title.rendered: Google Gemini AI Plus Student Offer: How to Claim It for Free

content.rendered:
Google has launched a new Back-to-School student offer that gives eligible students access to the Google AI Plus student plan at no cost for the promotional period.

The offer includes higher limits in Gemini, additional Google storage, and other AI-related benefits. If you are a college or university student, this offer can be useful for studying, research, coding, writing, and other academic work.

I recently redeemed the student offer myself. Since many students are facing difficulties during the verification and payment setup process, here is a complete step-by-step guide.

What Do You Get With the Google AI Plus Student Offer?

Eligible students can get several benefits through the offer, including:

  • 2X higher limits in Gemini
  • 400 GB of total Google storage
  • Storage that can be used across Google Photos, Google Drive, and Gmail
  • Access to additional Google AI features
  • Student-specific benefits included with the Google AI Plus plan

The exact benefits and eligibility requirements can vary, so check the offer page before completing the redemption.

How to Claim the Google Gemini Student Offer

Follow these steps to redeem the offer.

Step 1: Open the Student Offer Page

Open your browser and visit:

goo.gle/studentdeal

You can also access the offer through Google’s official student promotion page.

After opening the page, you should see an option such as:

“Claim Student Offer at no cost”

Click on it to continue.

Step 2: Select the Google AI Plus Student Offer

You will be taken to the Google AI Plus plan page.

Look for the “Get Student Offer” option and click on it.

Google will then ask you to verify your student status.

Step 3: Verify Your Student Status

Google uses SheerID to verify whether you are an eligible student.

Click “Continue” to begin the verification process.

Before starting, make sure you are signed in to the Google account you want to use for the offer.

If your institution provides a student email address, such as an address ending in .edu or .edu.in, keep that account signed in.

If you do not have an institutional email address, SheerID may provide alternative verification methods depending on your institution and eligibility.

Step 4: Enter Your Student Information

The verification page may ask you to provide information such as:

  • Country
  • College or university
  • First name
  • Last name
  • Date of birth
  • Personal email address

Enter the information exactly as it appears in your student records.

NOTE : ENTER YOUR EMAIL WHERE YOU WANT TO CLAIM THIS OFFER

For example, select India as your country if you are studying in India. Then search for and select your college or university.

Once you have entered the required information, click “Verify Student Status.”

Step 5: Complete SheerID Verification

If your institutional account is already signed in, SheerID may automatically detect it.

You may receive a request asking you to allow the verification process to access your student account.

Follow the instructions on the screen and provide the required permission.

If your student status is successfully verified, you will be redirected to the Google student offer page.

Step 6: Choose a Payment Method

After your student status has been verified, Google may ask you to add a payment method before activating the offer.

This can include options such as UPI or other supported payment methods.

In my case, I used UPI.

The reason UPI can be convenient is that it supports AutoPay, which can be managed or cancelled through your payment provider.

Step 7: Set Up UPI AutoPay

Select UPI and follow the instructions shown on the screen.

You may receive a QR code that you can scan using your preferred UPI app.

Complete the payment authorization process.

Google may make a small temporary verification charge, such as ₹2. This type of verification charge is generally reversed after verification, according to the offer flow.

Always check the amount shown on your own screen before approving a transaction.

Step 8: Finish the Activation

Once the payment method has been successfully added, your Google AI Plus student offer should be activated if you meet all eligibility requirements.

Click “Done” to finish the process.

You can then start using the benefits included with the student plan.

What If SheerID Cannot Verify You?

Some students may not get instant verification.

If this happens, check the following:

  • Make sure your name matches your student records.
  • Select the correct college or university.
  • Check that your date of birth is correct.
  • Use the correct institutional email if available.
  • Make sure you are using the Google account where you want the offer activated.
  • Follow any additional document verification instructions provided by SheerID.

If your institution does not appear in the verification system, check whether Google or SheerID provides another verification option.

Can You Cancel the Subscription Later?

If the student offer requires a payment method or AutoPay, check your Google subscription settings after activation.

If you do not want the subscription to continue after the promotional period, cancel it before the offer period ends.

Do not rely only on the fact that the current plan is free. Check the subscription terms and renewal date shown in your Google account.

Why This Offer Can Be Useful for Students

Students can use Gemini and other Google AI features for tasks such as:

  • Understanding difficult concepts
  • Summarizing study material
  • Generating practice questions
  • Improving writing
  • Learning programming
  • Debugging code
  • Research assistance
  • Brainstorming project ideas
  • Preparing presentations
  • Organizing study notes

The additional Google storage can also be useful if you regularly use Google Drive, Gmail, and Google Photos.

Important Things to Check Before Redeeming

Before you claim the offer, make sure you read the eligibility and promotion terms.

Also check:

  1. Whether your college or university is eligible.
  2. Whether the offer is available in your country.
  3. The promotional period.
  4. Which Google account will receive the benefit.
  5. Whether a payment method is required.
  6. When the subscription will renew or change to a paid plan.
  7. How to cancel the subscription if you do not want future charges.

also read : https://notesgallery.com/deloitte-recruitment-2026-2/

Final Steps

The overall process is simple:

  1. Open goo.gle/studentdeal.
  2. Select “Claim Student Offer at no cost.”
  3. Choose “Get Student Offer.”
  4. Start student verification through SheerID.
  5. Enter your college and personal details.
  6. Complete student verification.
  7. Add a supported payment method if required.
  8. Complete the UPI or payment authorization.
  9. Finish activation.
  10. Check your Google account to confirm that the student plan is active.

If you are an eligible student, this Google AI Plus student offer can give you access to additional Gemini limits, Google storage, and other benefits without paying the regular plan price during the promotional period.

Before signing up, always verify the current terms directly on Google’s student offer page because eligibility, pricing, benefits, and promotional dates can change.

content.rendered:
Welcome to the ultimate resource for AKTU Simulation & Modeling Notes. Whether you are preparing for your mid-semester tests or final exams, reviewing previous year papers is one of the most effective strategies to secure high marks. On this page, you will find comprehensive resources specifically curated for AKTU MCA Semester 3 students.

AKTU MCA Second Year Simulation & Modeling Notes Download

Use the table below to access year-wise PDFs. Click on the download links to get the materials directly to your device.

Download Simulation & Modeling Notes

Note:
PDF 1 ≠ Unit 1. Each collection may contain complete,
unit-wise, part-wise, or mixed notes.

About Simulation & Modeling

Simulation & Modeling is a core theory subject in the AKTU MCA Semester 3 curriculum. This subject introduces students to fundamental concepts that form the foundation for advanced subjects in later semesters. A thorough understanding of Simulation & Modeling is essential not only for passing the semester examination but also for building the conceptual base required throughout the MCA programme. The subject covers both theoretical principles and their practical applications, making it important to study from multiple resources including standard textbooks, class notes, and previous year question papers.

Students who dedicate focused time to understanding the core concepts of Simulation & Modeling often find that the subject becomes significantly easier as the semester progresses. The examination pattern for Simulation & Modeling typically includes short-answer questions, long-answer questions, and numerical or application-based problems. Reviewing the AKTU Simulation & Modeling PYQs reveals which types of questions appear most frequently and gives you a clear idea of what to expect in your own examination.

Why Previous Year Question Papers Are Useful

Solving previous year question papers is one of the most effective exam preparation strategies recommended by toppers and faculty alike. Here is why Simulation & Modeling PYQs are particularly valuable for AKTU MCA students:

  • Understand the Exam Pattern: PYQs reveal how questions are distributed across units, the format of long-answer versus short-answer questions, and the total marks for each section. This helps you plan your time effectively during the actual examination.
  • Identify Repeated Topics: Certain concepts and questions appear repeatedly across multiple years. Identifying these high-frequency topics allows you to prioritise your revision and ensure that the most commonly tested material is thoroughly covered.
  • Gauge Difficulty Level: Solving past papers gives you an accurate sense of how difficult the AKTU Simulation & Modeling examination typically is. This helps you set realistic expectations and avoid being surprised during the exam.
  • Practice Time Management: Working through a full question paper under timed conditions trains you to manage the three-hour examination window effectively. Many students lose marks not because they lack knowledge but because they run out of time.
  • Build Confidence: Successfully solving previous papers boosts confidence. When you enter the examination hall knowing that you have already solved similar questions, your performance improves significantly.

Important Topics and Preparation Areas

When preparing Simulation & Modeling for your AKTU MCA Semester 3 examination, focus on the units that carry the most weightage in the question paper. Based on an analysis of previous years papers, the following preparation areas are consistently important:

  • Core theoretical concepts covered in Unit I and Unit II of the Simulation & Modeling syllabus
  • Definitions, classifications, and key terminology that appear frequently in short-answer sections
  • Diagrams, reactions, or numerical derivations that are commonly asked as long-answer questions
  • Application-based questions that test understanding rather than rote memorisation
  • Revision of previous units as questions often draw connections between multiple topics

Make sure you have a copy of the official AKTU MCA Semester 3 syllabus for Simulation & Modeling and cross-reference it with the topics that appear in the PYQs. This will help you identify any gaps in your preparation well before the examination date.

How to Use Previous Year Papers Effectively

Simply downloading the Simulation & Modeling PYQs is not enough. Here is a step-by-step approach to using them effectively for your AKTU MCA semester examination:

  1. Complete Your Syllabus First: Before attempting PYQs, ensure that you have studied all units of the Simulation & Modeling syllabus. Attempting papers before completing the syllabus leads to confusion and discouragement.
  2. Solve Without Referring to Notes: Attempt each paper under exam conditions without looking at your notes. This simulates the actual examination environment and reveals your true level of preparation.
  3. Review and Self-Evaluate: After completing each paper, check your answers against your textbook and notes. Note the questions you answered incorrectly or could not attempt.
  4. Identify Weak Areas: Look for patterns in your incorrect answers. If you consistently struggle with certain units, spend extra revision time on those topics before the examination.
  5. Repeat With Recent Papers Last: Start with older papers and work forward chronologically, finishing with the most recent available paper. This gives you a sense of how the paper pattern has evolved.

Step-by-Step Download Instructions

Downloading the Simulation & Modeling previous year papers from this page is straightforward and requires no registration or payment:

  1. Scroll to the download table above on this page.
  2. Locate the academic year for which you want the question paper.
  3. Click the download button in the relevant semester column.
  4. The PDF will open in a new tab or download automatically depending on your browser settings.
  5. Save the file to your device for offline access during your preparation.

Exam Preparation Strategy

A structured preparation strategy significantly improves your chances of scoring well in the Simulation & Modeling examination. Begin your preparation at least four to six weeks before the examination date. Divide the syllabus into manageable weekly goals and stick to a daily study schedule. During the final two weeks, shift your focus entirely to revision and PYQ practice. Avoid studying new material in the last few days before the examination and instead concentrate on reinforcing what you already know through repeated practice.

Use the AKTU Simulation & Modeling question papers as a revision tool rather than a shortcut. Understand the concepts behind each answer rather than memorising model answers verbatim. Examiners can tell the difference between a student who understands the material and one who has simply memorised answers without comprehension.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Starting PYQs Too Late: Many students attempt previous year papers only in the final week before the exam. By this stage, there is not enough time to revise weak areas identified through the papers.
  • Skipping Difficult Questions: It is tempting to only solve questions you already know how to answer. Make sure to attempt challenging questions and learn from your mistakes rather than avoiding them entirely.
  • Ignoring the Syllabus: Some students focus only on PYQs and neglect portions of the syllabus that have not appeared in recent years. New topics can always be introduced by the university without prior notice.
  • Not Practising Structured Writing: In theory papers, presentation and structured writing matter. Practice writing complete, well-organised answers rather than just knowing the concepts informally.
  • Over-Relying on a Single Source: PYQs are one preparation tool among several. Combine them with your class notes, standard textbooks recommended by AKTU, and solved examples from reference books.

You can download unit-wise handwritten and typed notes directly from this page in PDF format.

Are these notes strictly according to the AKTU syllabus?

Yes, these notes cover all important units and topics prescribed by the latest AKTU syllabus.

Can I clear my semester exams using these notes?

Yes, combining these notes with previous year question papers is the best strategy to score high marks in semester exams.

Are these Simulation & Modeling notes free to download?

Yes, all resources on NotesGallery are completely free to view and download.

We regularly update our study materials and add new contributions from university toppers.

title.rendered: Deloitte Recruitment 2026: Associate Analyst Automation Testing Job for BE/BTech Freshers

content.rendered:
Deloitte is hiring an Associate Analyst for its Automation Testing team in Bengaluru. The opening is aimed at fresh graduates and candidates with up to 2 years of experience.

If you have a BE or BTech degree and are interested in software testing, Selenium, Java or Python, this could be a good entry-level opportunity to consider.

Deloitte Associate Analyst Recruitment 2026

About the Job

As an Associate Analyst, you will be part of Deloitte’s Quality Engineering team. The work will involve testing applications, creating automated test scripts, finding software issues, and working with developers to fix them.

The role is suitable for someone who wants to start a career in QA, automation testing, or software quality engineering.

You do not need several years of industry experience for this position. Deloitte has mentioned 0-2 years of experience, making it relevant for freshers as well.

What Will You Do?

Your day-to-day work may include:

  • Understanding application requirements.
  • Preparing test cases and test scenarios.
  • Creating and maintaining automation scripts.
  • Testing web and API applications.
  • Performing functional and regression testing.
  • Carrying out smoke and sanity testing.
  • Reporting and tracking bugs.
  • Checking whether reported issues have been fixed.
  • Working with developers and other project team members.
  • Taking part in Agile meetings.
  • Maintaining testing documents and reports.

Skills Required

Deloitte is looking for candidates who have a basic understanding of software testing and programming.

The main skills mentioned in the job description are:

  • STLC and SDLC
  • Selenium WebDriver
  • Java or Python
  • API testing
  • Postman or REST Assured
  • SQL
  • Database concepts
  • Git
  • Debugging
  • Problem-solving
  • Good communication

You do not have to know every tool listed in the job description perfectly. However, you should be comfortable explaining the skills and projects you mention on your resume.

Preferred Skills

Knowledge of these technologies can give you an advantage:

  • TestNG
  • JUnit
  • Cucumber
  • BDD
  • Jenkins
  • CI/CD
  • Agile/Scrum

If you have completed a college project or internship related to automation testing, include it on your resume.

Eligibility

You can consider applying if you meet these basic requirements:

  • You have a BE or BTech degree.
  • You have 0-2 years of experience.
  • You understand basic software testing concepts.
  • You know Java or Python at a basic level.
  • You have knowledge of Selenium WebDriver.

title.rendered: AKTU ISGBB Initiative: Workshops for Student Innovators

content.rendered:
Innovation Hub Uttar Pradesh at Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University has invited affiliated institutions to participate in the ISGBB Initiative, short for Innovations for Social Good and Better Bharat, and host Entrepreneurship & Innovation Workshops for students and startups.

The initiative is being supported by Innovation Hub Uttar Pradesh in collaboration with Bharat Cares. It is designed to nurture student innovators, early-stage entrepreneurs and social-impact solutions by connecting academia, industry, startups and the wider innovation ecosystem.

ISGBB Initiative Overview

Particular Details
Initiative Innovations for Social Good and Better Bharat (ISGBB)
Organiser/Support Innovation Hub Uttar Pradesh in collaboration with Bharat Cares
University Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University
Circular Date 19 August 2026
Reference Number AKTU/IH/2026/732
Target Audience Student innovators, early-stage entrepreneurs and startups
Activity Entrepreneurship & Innovation Workshops
Host AKTU-affiliated institutions
Cost per Workshop ₹5,700
Cost Bearer Bharat Cares
Participation Fee No fee for host institution or students

What Is the ISGBB Initiative?

The Innovations for Social Good and Better Bharat (ISGBB) initiative focuses on encouraging young innovators and aspiring entrepreneurs to work on real-world problems and develop practical solutions.

According to the official communication, the programme aims to help participants gain access to:

  • Mentorship
  • Validation
  • Ecosystem linkages
  • Opportunities to showcase ideas

The initiative also seeks to connect academic institutions with industry, startups and the broader innovation ecosystem.

Who Is the Initiative Meant For?

The official communication highlights the following groups:

  • Student innovators
  • Early-stage entrepreneurs
  • Aspiring entrepreneurs
  • Startups
  • Teams working on social-impact solutions

The circular does not prescribe a particular academic branch, course, semester or graduating batch.

What Are Institutions Being Asked to Do?

AKTU-affiliated institutions have been invited to host the workshops on their own premises for the benefit of students and startups.

Institutions are expected to:

  • Nominate themselves to host the programme
  • Facilitate the workshop at their institution
  • Support participation of students and startups
  • Nominate a concerned person for further coordination

The communication is addressed to the Directors and Heads of all AKTU-affiliated institutions in Uttar Pradesh.

Workshop Budget

The circular provides an indicative budget of ₹5,700 per workshop.

Budget Head Amount
Mentor Honorarium ₹3,000
Program Expenses at Workshop ₹1,500
Travel & Miscellaneous Expenses ₹1,200
Total ₹5,700

The mentor honorarium is intended for the mentor or resource person, while programme expenses cover collaterals and knowledge materials. Travel and miscellaneous expenses include travel and incidental costs.

Is There Any Fee for Students or Colleges?

No.

The circular clearly states that Bharat Cares will bear the full ₹5,700 cost per workshop.

No financial contribution or participation fee is required from:

  • The host institution
  • Students

This means affiliated institutions can host the workshop without contributing to the stated workshop budget.

What Participants Can Gain

The initiative is intended to help young innovators and aspiring entrepreneurs:

  • Identify real-world challenges
  • Develop innovative solutions
  • Access mentorship
  • Receive validation
  • Connect with the innovation ecosystem
  • Get opportunities to showcase their ideas

These benefits are specifically mentioned as part of the initiative’s objectives.

The circular provides the following participation link:

https://bit.ly/ISGBB

Institutions interested in hosting the workshop can use the participation link or the QR code provided in the official communication.

The institution should also nominate a concerned person who can coordinate further regarding the workshop.

Event Date

The circular provides the participation link but does not mention a final deadline for submitting nominations.

What AKTU Institutions Should Keep in Mind

Affiliated institutions interested in participating should note:

  • The programme focuses on innovation, entrepreneurship and social-impact solutions.
  • Workshops are intended for the benefit of students and startups.
  • Institutions can nominate themselves to host the event.
  • A concerned coordinator should be nominated by the institution.
  • Bharat Cares will bear the full workshop cost of ₹5,700.
  • No participation fee or institutional financial contribution is required.
  • The circular does not state a final deadline.

The communication carries reference number AKTU/IH/2026/732 and is dated 19 August 2026.

It is issued by Innovation Hub Uttar Pradesh, Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Lucknow, and addressed to the Directors and Heads of all AKTU-affiliated institutions in Uttar Pradesh.

title.rendered: AKTU Tree Plantation 2026: 500 Saplings per College

content.rendered:
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University has issued instructions regarding the AKTU Tree Plantation Campaign 2026 for the academic year 2026–27. The circular asks institutions associated with AKTU to participate in the state plantation programme and work toward the plantation targets assigned under the wider Uttar Pradesh tree plantation campaign.

The state-level campaign has a target of planting 35 crore saplings during 2026–27. For institutions associated with AKTU, the university has set a target of 500 saplings per institution and has asked colleges to ensure proper implementation, monitoring and reporting of plantation activities.

AKTU Tree Plantation Campaign 2026 Overview

Particular Details
University Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University
Circular Date 23 July 2026
Academic Year 2026–27
Campaign Tree Plantation Campaign / Vriksharopan Mahabhiyan 2026
State-Level Target 35 crore saplings
Target for AKTU Institutions 500 saplings per institution
Special Campaign Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam
Major Plantation Date Referenced 12 July 2026
Applicable To Institutions associated with AKTU
Reporting Plantation progress and compliance to be maintained and submitted

What Has AKTU Announced?

AKTU has directed the heads of its associated institutions to ensure participation in the tree plantation programme for 2026–27.

The university communication refers to instructions issued by the Uttar Pradesh Technical Education Department and the Environment, Forest and Climate Change Department regarding implementation of the state’s large-scale plantation campaign.

Institutions are expected to follow the prescribed plantation directions, achieve their assigned targets and maintain the required records so that consolidated compliance information can be provided to the government.

500 Saplings Target for Each AKTU Institution

A major requirement in the circular is the plantation target assigned to institutions associated with the university.

Each institution has been given a target of:

500 saplings during the 2026–27 plantation campaign.

Colleges and institutes are therefore expected to organise plantation activities on their campuses or other suitable locations and ensure that the assigned target is achieved.

The circular also stresses that plantation should not be treated only as a one-day activity. Institutions are expected to ensure the survival, protection and maintenance of planted saplings.

35 Crore Tree Plantation Target in Uttar Pradesh

The AKTU circular refers to the Uttar Pradesh government’s wider target of planting 35 crore saplings during 2026–27.

Government review meetings were held under the chairmanship of the Chief Minister regarding preparation and implementation of this large-scale plantation drive.

As part of the campaign, 12 July 2026 was identified for a major one-day plantation programme across the state.

The attached government directions called for the plantation of 35 crore saplings on that day, with plantation activities scheduled from 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM, or according to timing determined by the respective District Magistrate.

Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam Campaign

The plantation programme is also linked with the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” campaign.

Under the instructions referenced by AKTU, plantation activities are to be conducted under this theme as part of Vriksharopan Mahabhiyan 2026.

Institutions are expected to encourage participation by students, faculty members and other stakeholders so that tree plantation becomes a wider public and institutional activity.

What AKTU Colleges Need to Do

AKTU-associated institutions are expected to take several actions under the plantation campaign:

  • Participate in the plantation programme for 2026–27.
  • Work toward planting 500 saplings per institution.
  • Conduct plantation activities under the prescribed campaign guidelines.
  • Encourage participation by students and institutional staff.
  • Maintain information about the saplings planted.
  • Ensure geotagging of plantation locations or planted saplings as instructed.
  • Maintain records of plantation numbers and activities.
  • Take steps for the protection and maintenance of planted saplings.
  • Submit or make available plantation-related information in the prescribed format.
  • Follow further instructions issued by the university and concerned government departments.

Participation of Students and Educational Institutions

The government directions attached with the circular give special importance to the participation of school and college students.

Universities, colleges, medical colleges, schools and other educational institutions are expected to actively involve students in plantation activities.

Institutions may also organise awareness programmes and workshops related to tree plantation and environmental protection to encourage meaningful participation.

For AKTU-affiliated institutions, this means colleges should involve their academic community rather than limiting implementation only to administrative staff.

Plantation of Suitable Tree Species

The attached government directions encourage plantation of a wide range of useful, native and environmentally important species.

Species referred to in the instructions include:

  • Peepal
  • Pakad
  • Banyan
  • Neem
  • Jamun
  • Imli
  • Bael
  • Arjun
  • Sahjan
  • Mango
  • Mahua
  • Amla

The directions also encourage plantation of shade-giving, fruit-bearing, medicinal and environmentally important species.

Native species are to be given preference in plantation activities.

Geotagging and Monitoring of Plantation

Monitoring is an important part of the campaign.

The directions require plantation sites and planted saplings to be geotagged so that plantation activity can be properly recorded and monitored.

Institutions are also expected to maintain information about plantation progress and help ensure that the planted saplings survive after the initial plantation activity.

This means the campaign involves both planting and subsequent monitoring rather than simply recording the number of saplings planted.

Protection and Maintenance of Saplings

Institutions are expected to make arrangements for protecting planted saplings.

Depending on local requirements, these measures may include:

  • Fencing
  • Tree guards
  • Other protective arrangements
  • Watering
  • Regular maintenance

The government directions give priority to the survival and upkeep of planted trees after plantation.

Plantation Progress Reporting

AKTU has asked institutions to provide compliance and plantation-related information so that the university can consolidate the data and report progress to the concerned authorities.

The circular contains a Google Form link for submitting the required information.

The university has also instructed concerned officials to collect plantation information through the prescribed ERP format and maintain a plantation count register.

Institutions should therefore ensure that their reported plantation figures match their actual plantation activities and records.

Annexure of Institutions

The circular includes a detailed annexure containing institute codes and names of institutions associated with AKTU.

The annexure extends across multiple pages and contains 722 institution entries, covering engineering, management, architecture, pharmacy and other affiliated institutions.

Institutions included in the annexure should review the university’s plantation instructions and ensure that their assigned responsibilities are completed.

Important Dates

AKTU Circular Referenced 12 June 2026
State-Level Review Meeting 3 July 2026
Further Review Meeting 6 July 2026
Major One-Day Plantation Programme 12 July 2026
Technical Education Department Communication 17 July 2026
Current AKTU Circular 23 July 2026
Campaign Period 2026–27

Key Points for AKTU Institutions

Institutions should particularly note the following:

  • The plantation campaign applies during 2026–27.
  • Uttar Pradesh has set a statewide target of 35 crore saplings.
  • AKTU-associated institutions have been assigned a target of 500 saplings per institution.
  • Plantation activities are linked with Vriksharopan Mahabhiyan 2026 and Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam.
  • Students and institutional staff should be encouraged to participate.
  • Plantation records and progress should be properly maintained.
  • Geotagging of plantation activity is required under the referenced instructions.
  • Protection, watering and maintenance of planted saplings should receive priority.
  • Institutions are expected to provide compliance information to the university.

Official Circular Details

The AKTU circular is dated 23 July 2026 and concerns the successful implementation of the tree plantation campaign for the year 2026–27.

It is addressed to the Chairpersons, Directors and Principals of institutions associated with Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University.

The circular refers to earlier communications of the Uttar Pradesh Technical Education Department and state Environment, Forest and Climate Change Department regarding the 35 crore plantation campaign.

The communication is signed by Reena Singh, Registrar, and asks concerned institutions and university officials to ensure proper implementation, collection of plantation information and maintenance of records.

Official Circular Document

Official AKTU Circular and Website

Download Official Circular PDFVisit AKTU Official Website

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

What is the AKTU Tree Plantation Campaign 2026?

The **AKTU Tree Plantation Campaign 2026** is AKTU’s institutional plantation initiative for 2026–27 under the wider Uttar Pradesh tree plantation campaign. Affiliated institutions have been asked to participate and achieve their assigned plantation targets.

How many saplings does each AKTU institution have to plant?

The circular sets a target of **500 saplings per institution** for institutions associated with AKTU during the 2026–27 plantation programme.

What is the 35 crore plantation target?

The Uttar Pradesh government has set a statewide target of planting **35 crore saplings** as part of the 2026–27 tree plantation campaign.

What is Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam?

**Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam** is the campaign theme referenced in the plantation instructions. Institutions are encouraged to carry out plantation activities under this theme as part of Vriksharopan Mahabhiyan 2026.

Do AKTU colleges need to geotag planted saplings?

Yes. The directions referred to in the circular require geotagging of plantation sites or planted saplings for monitoring and reporting purposes.

Are students expected to participate in the plantation campaign?

Yes. The government instructions give priority to participation by students of educational institutions, and AKTU institutions are expected to encourage student involvement in plantation activities.

Do colleges need to report their plantation progress?

Yes. Institutions are expected to maintain plantation records and provide the required compliance information so that AKTU can consolidate and forward the plantation progress to the concerned authorities.

title.rendered: AKTU Re-Admitted Students 2026-27: New A-Series Curriculum Mandatory for Failed B.Tech First-Year Students

content.rendered:
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Uttar Pradesh, has issued an important notice for B.Tech students who are being re-admitted in the first year during the 2026-27 academic session. The university has introduced a new course structure, known as the A-Series, for the 2026-27 session.

According to the official notice dated 18 August 2026, students who were previously admitted to B.Tech First Year under the earlier B-Series curriculum and are now re-admitted because of failure will have to complete their studies under the new A-Series curriculum.

The notice has been issued to institutions affiliated with AKTU and includes specific instructions regarding re-admitted students, failed students and students covered under different course structures.

AKTU Re-Admission 2026-27: What Has Changed?

AKTU introduced the AICTE Model Curriculum-based B-Series course structure from the 2022-23 session. The university has now introduced a revised course structure and ordinance, referred to as the A-Series, for the 2026-27 academic session.

The main change affects students who were admitted earlier but could not successfully complete their B.Tech First Year and are now required to reappear or register again in the 2026-27 session.

Such students will be treated as Re-Admitted students and will have to follow the new A-Series curriculum.

Who Will Be Affected by the New A-Series Curriculum?

The notice mainly covers students who meet the conditions mentioned by AKTU for the 2026-27 session.

1. Students who failed B.Tech First Year

Students who were admitted to B.Tech First Year in the 2025-26 session or an earlier session and could not pass the first year because of failure will be required to register as Re-Admitted students in 2026-27 if they want to complete their B.Tech First Year.

These students will have to complete their B.Tech First Year according to the new A-Series curriculum applicable from 2026-27.

The university has also stated that these students must complete the applicable B.Tech curriculum according to the new structure. They cannot simply continue their entire course under the previous curriculum.

What Happens to Students Who Were Earlier Under B-Series?

Students who originally entered B.Tech under the B-Series curriculum may now be shifted to the A-Series if they are re-admitted in 2026-27.

The official notice specifically states that students re-admitted to B.Tech First Year in 2026-27 will be governed by the new A-Series course structure and ordinance.

This means students should carefully check their registration, examination form and course requirements with their respective college.

Important Rule for Failed Students

One of the most important points in the notice is that a student who failed B.Tech First Year and is re-admitted in 2026-27 cannot continue the complete B.Tech programme under the old course structure.

The undertaking attached to the university notice clearly states that the student will be governed by the new A-Series structure from the 2026-27 session. The student will also have to complete the subsequent years of the B.Tech programme under the A-Series structure.

Therefore, students should not assume that they will remain under the previous B-Series curriculum after re-admission.

What About Ex-Students?

The university notice also contains provisions concerning B.Tech First Year students treated as Ex-Students in 2026-27. Such students may have to complete their pending B.Tech First Year requirements according to the applicable instructions and course structure specified by the university.

Students in this category should contact their college or institute to confirm their individual status before completing registration or examination-related formalities.

What About Students Who Failed Other Years?

The notice also provides instructions for students who were unsuccessful in their B.Tech programme and need to complete pending academic requirements.

The university has instructed affiliated institutions to inform the concerned students about the applicable course structure and ensure compliance with the instructions for the 2026-27 session.

Because the exact academic situation can differ between students, those with pending subjects should verify their status with their institute.

Lateral Entry Students

The notice also mentions B.Tech Second Year students admitted through Lateral Entry.

For students admitted to B.Tech Second Year through Lateral Entry in 2026-27, the applicable curriculum will depend on the relevant admission session and course structure. The notice distinguishes between students connected with the earlier B-Series structure and students covered by the new A-Series structure.

Students entering through Lateral Entry should therefore confirm which course structure applies to their admission session.

Undertaking Is Mandatory for Certain Re-Admitted Students

AKTU has attached an Undertaking/Declaration form with the official notice.

The annexure states that the undertaking must be submitted by every B.Tech First Year student who failed and is registering or reappearing in B.Tech First Year during the 2026-27 session as a Re-Admitted student. These students will be governed by the new A-Series course structure.

The form asks students to provide details such as:

  • Student name
  • Father’s name
  • Date of birth
  • Roll number
  • Enrollment number
  • Institute name
  • Original B.Tech First Year admission session
  • Re-admission session

The form also requires the student’s declaration and signature. It must be countersigned by the Head of the concerned Institute, Director or Principal.

What Students Should Do Now

If you are a B.Tech student affected by this notice, you should take the following steps:

  1. Confirm whether you are classified as a Re-Admitted student for 2026-27.
  2. Contact your college administration or examination section.
  3. Check which course structure applies to your registration.
  4. Complete the required registration process under the A-Series where applicable.
  5. Submit the Undertaking/Declaration if required.
  6. Check your examination form carefully before submission.
  7. Keep a copy of all submitted documents for your records.

AKTU has specifically asked affiliated institutions to inform the concerned students about these arrangements and ensure that the required undertaking is obtained from eligible Re-Admitted students.

AKTU A-Series vs B-Series for Re-Admitted Students

The key difference for affected students is the applicable course structure.

The table above summarizes the specific transition described in the university notice. Students should follow their college’s instructions for individual cases.

Important Point for AKTU Students

The most important message from this notification is that re-admitted B.Tech First Year students in the 2026-27 session should not assume that their old course structure will continue.

If you failed B.Tech First Year and are being re-admitted in 2026-27, the university has stated that you will be governed by the new A-Series course structure. The attached undertaking also confirms that subsequent years of the B.Tech programme will have to be completed under the new A-Series structure.

Students should therefore complete the required formalities through their college and carefully check all information before submitting their registration or examination forms.

AKTU Re-Admission 2026-27: FAQs

Is A-Series mandatory for Re-Admitted B.Tech First Year students?

Yes. According to the official AKTU notice, eligible students who are re-admitted to B.Tech First Year in the 2026-27 session will be governed by the new A-Series course structure.

I failed B.Tech First Year. Will I follow the old B-Series syllabus?

If you are being re-admitted in B.Tech First Year in the 2026-27 session under the conditions covered by this notice, you will be governed by the new A-Series course structure.

Is an undertaking required?

Yes, the attached undertaking states that it is mandatory for every eligible failed B.Tech First Year student who registers or reappears as a Re-Admitted student in 2026-27.

Can I complete my remaining B.Tech years under the old course structure?

The undertaking specifically states that a Re-Admitted student cannot continue or complete the B.Tech programme under the previous course structure. The student will be governed by the A-Series structure.

When was the AKTU notice issued?

The notice is dated 18 August 2026 and was issued from Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow.

Final Update

AKTU has introduced important changes for B.Tech students who are re-admitted to First Year during the 2026-27 session. Students covered by the university’s Re-Admission rules will have to follow the new A-Series course structure.

If you are a failed B.Tech First Year student who is returning through Re-Admission, check your status with your college and complete the required undertaking and registration formalities. The official notice makes it clear that eligible Re-Admitted students will be governed by the A-Series curriculum for their remaining B.Tech studies.

title.rendered: DigiLocker Marksheet & Degree Download 2026: Here’s How Students Can Get Their Documents

content.rendered:
Students looking for their marksheets, degrees, diplomas, or other academic records can access them digitally through DigiLocker when the concerned university, board, or educational institution has made the documents available through the National Academic Depository (NAD).

The official NAD-DigiLocker instructions provided in the attached document explain how students can find, view, download, verify, and share their academic records using both the DigiLocker website and mobile app.

If you need your marksheet or degree for admission, employment, higher studies, or document verification, this guide explains the complete process in simple steps.

Official NAD-DigiLocker Notice

The official communication states that students’ educational records, including degrees and marksheets, are made available on DigiLocker through the National Academic Depository. It also asks educational institutions to display and circulate the instructions so students can easily access their digital academic records.

What Is NAD-DigiLocker?

DigiLocker provides a digital platform for accessing documents that have been issued to a user’s account.

For academic records, the National Academic Depository (NAD) works with DigiLocker to make records provided by universities, boards, and educational institutions available digitally.

The official infographic explains that academic documents available through DigiLocker can be digitally signed and verified online.

One important point is that DigiLocker does not create your university marksheet or degree. The concerned institution must first provide the academic record through the supported system.

Which Academic Documents Can You Get on DigiLocker?

The documents available to you depend on the records provided by your university, board, or institution.

The official flowcharts include examples such as:

  • Marksheet
  • Degree
  • Diploma
  • Certificate
  • Other academic records

If your institution has not provided a particular document, it may not appear in DigiLocker.

How to Download Your Marksheet or Degree from DigiLocker

The DigiLocker website provides a step-by-step process for finding your academic record and downloading the available document.

DigiLocker Website Download Process

The official flowchart covers the process from signing in to DigiLocker to searching for the issuer, selecting the document, entering academic details, viewing the record, and downloading it.

Step 1: Open the DigiLocker Website

Visit the DigiLocker website and sign in to your account.

The official flowchart begins with visiting the DigiLocker website.

Step 2: Sign In or Register

If you already have a DigiLocker account, sign in.

If you are using DigiLocker for the first time, complete the registration process.

The provided instructions include mobile number and OTP verification as part of the account access process.

Step 3: Complete the Required Verification

After signing in, complete the verification required for your account.

Make sure your account information is correct before searching for your academic record.

Step 4: Find Your University or Board

Go to the section for finding issued academic documents and search for the institution that issued your record.

Depending on your document, the issuer could be:

  • University
  • Board
  • Education Department
  • Other authorized institution

Select the correct issuer.

Step 5: Choose Your Document

Select the type of academic record you want to obtain.

For example:

  • Marksheet
  • Degree
  • Diploma
  • Certificate

The options shown to you depend on the documents provided by your issuer.

Step 6: Enter Your Academic Details

DigiLocker may ask for information required to identify your academic record.

The official flowchart includes details such as:

  • Roll Number
  • Year
  • Session
  • Registration Number
  • Other required information

Enter the details carefully and select Get Document.

Step 7: Get Your Document

If the record is available, DigiLocker will fetch it and make it available in your account.

The document will appear in the Issued Documents section.

Step 8: View Your Marksheet or Degree

Open the document from Issued Documents.

Check the details shown on your academic record before saving or sharing it.

Step 9: Download the PDF

Use the Download option to save the available document.

The official flowchart shows the document being downloaded as a PDF file.

How to Download a Marksheet or Degree from the DigiLocker App

You can also access your academic documents through the DigiLocker mobile app.

The mobile process is slightly different in terms of navigation, but the basic steps remain similar.

DigiLocker App Download Process

The third page of the attached document shows the complete mobile workflow, including app installation, login, document search, document availability, viewing, downloading, and sharing.

Step 1: Install the DigiLocker App

Install the DigiLocker mobile app from the relevant app store.

Step 2: Log In

Open the app and enter your mobile number.

Complete OTP verification.

The flowchart also shows the option to enter a security PIN if one has already been set.

Step 3: Open Issued Documents

After logging in, open the Issued Documents section.

This is where documents issued to your DigiLocker account can be accessed.

Step 4: Select Get Your Document

Select Get Your Document.

Search for your university, board, education department, or other relevant issuer.

Then select the document you want to obtain.

Step 5: Enter the Required Information

Enter the details requested by the issuer.

These may include your roll number, enrollment number, registration number, year, session, or other academic information.

After entering the details, select Get Document.

Step 6: Check Whether the Document Is Available

If the record is available, DigiLocker will fetch it into your account.

If the document is not available, the official flowchart directs students to contact the concerned issuer, such as their university or board.

Step 7: View the Document

Once the document has been issued, open it from the Issued Documents section.

Review the information shown on your marksheet, degree, or other academic record.

Step 8: Download the Document

Tap the Download option to save the document.

The official mobile flowchart shows the document being downloaded as a PDF.

Step 9: Share the Document

The final stage of the mobile flowchart also includes an option to share the document.

The document can also be printed when required.

What If Your Marksheet or Degree Is Not Showing?

This is one of the most common issues students may face when searching for an academic record.

If your document is not available, first check whether you have selected the correct issuer and entered the correct academic details.

Check:

  • University or board name
  • Document type
  • Roll number
  • Registration number
  • Enrollment number, where applicable
  • Academic year
  • Session

If the document still does not appear, contact the concerned university, board, or educational institution.

The official mobile flowchart specifically directs students to contact the concerned issuer when the requested document is unavailable.

How Are Academic Records Added to DigiLocker?

Academic records are provided by universities, boards, and educational institutions.

The official infographic explains that institutions upload academic records to DigiLocker through NAD. Once the records are available, students can access them through their DigiLocker accounts.

This is why one student’s marksheet may be available while another student’s record is not yet visible. The availability depends on the concerned institution and the records it has provided.

Can DigiLocker Academic Documents Be Verified?

Yes. The official infographic explains that DigiLocker academic documents can be verified digitally.

The document can be verified using its QR code or through the DigiLocker verification facility.

The infographic also describes the documents as digitally signed, providing a way to verify the record against the issuing institution.

Why Students Should Keep Their DigiLocker Documents Ready

Digital academic records can be useful when you need to provide your educational information quickly.

Depending on the requirement, an available DigiLocker document may help when you need to:

  • Submit an academic record
  • Provide a marksheet
  • Provide a degree record
  • Share an academic document
  • Verify an educational record
  • Keep a digital copy for your records

The provided flowchart also includes sharing and printing options for accessed documents.

also read : https://notesgallery.com/ai-prompt-to-humanize-ai-writing/

Important Things to Remember

Before trying to fetch your document, keep your academic information available.

  • Select the correct issuer.
  • Choose the correct document type.
  • Enter your academic details accurately.
  • Keep your roll number available.
  • Keep your registration or enrollment number available.
  • Check the academic year and session.
  • Look in Issued Documents after fetching the record.
  • If the record is unavailable, contact the concerned institution.
  • Use the available verification facility when document verification is required.

DigiLocker Marksheet and Degree FAQs

Can I download my marksheet from DigiLocker?

Yes, if your university, board, or educational institution has made the academic record available through the supported NAD-DigiLocker system.

Can I download my degree from DigiLocker?

You can access your degree through DigiLocker if the concerned institution has provided the degree record through the supported system.

What information is needed to fetch a marksheet?

The exact requirements depend on the issuer. The official flowchart includes information such as roll number, year, session, and registration number.

Why can’t I find my marksheet on DigiLocker?

Your institution may not have made the record available yet, or the details entered during the search may not match the issuer’s records.

Check your details and issuer selection. If the document is still unavailable, contact the concerned university or board.

Can DigiLocker documents be verified online?

The official infographic explains that available academic documents can be verified using a QR code or DigiLocker’s verification facility.

Can I download my marksheet using the DigiLocker app?

Yes. The official mobile flowchart shows the process of logging in, finding the issuer, entering the required information, fetching the document, viewing it, downloading it, and sharing it.

Final Word

For students, DigiLocker offers a convenient way to access academic records that have been provided through the National Academic Depository.

The process is straightforward. Sign in through the DigiLocker website or app, find your university or board, select the required document, enter the requested details, and fetch the record. If the document is available, you can view and download it through the options provided by DigiLocker.

If your marksheet or degree is not available, check your details first. If the problem continues, contact the concerned institution because the academic record must be provided by the relevant issuer.

title.rendered: Best AI Prompt to Humanize AI Writing: Free Prompt to Make ChatGPT Text Sound Natural

content.rendered:
AI can write an article in seconds. The problem starts when the finished article sounds like it was written by a machine.

You may see the same phrases again and again. The introduction feels too long. Every section follows the same pattern. The writing uses words you would never normally use.

This is common with ChatGPT and other AI writing tools.

The good news is you do not need an expensive AI humanizer to improve the writing.

A good writing prompt can give the AI clear instructions about sentence length, tone, vocabulary, formatting, and structure. You can then make a few edits yourself before publishing.

Short Summery of post is Here 
• Make AI-generated text feel more human
• Remove repetitive and robotic phrasing
• Keep the original meaning and information
• Make the writing sound natural and conversational
• Works with ChatGPT and other AI tools

In this guide, you will get a free prompt to humanize AI writing, examples of how to use it, and practical tips for making AI-assisted content sound more natural.

READ NEXT

7 AI Skills You Need for Jobs in 2026

Learn the AI skills that can help you stay competitive in the 2026 job market.

Read article →
↗

Why Does AI Writing Sound So Similar?

AI tools learn patterns from large amounts of text. When you give them a broad instruction, they often produce writing that follows familiar patterns.

You might notice:

  • Long introductions before getting to the point
  • Repeated phrases
  • Generic explanations
  • Too many headings
  • Excessive adjectives
  • Unnecessary conclusions
  • Overly formal language
  • Marketing-style phrases
  • Repetitive sentence structures
  • Too much formatting

For example, an AI-generated sentence might be:

“Artificial intelligence is revolutionizing the ever-evolving landscape of content creation.”

A normal reader would understand this more easily:

“AI is changing how people create content.”

The second sentence is shorter. It says the same thing. It also avoids unnecessary wording.

The Free AI Prompt to Humanize Writing

You can use the following prompt with ChatGPT or another large language model.

The prompt tells the AI to use simple language, shorter sentences, active voice, specific examples, and a more natural tone.

It also tells the model what to avoid.

Caption:

Copy this prompt:

# FOLLOW THIS WRITING STYLE:

• Use clear, simple language.
• Keep the writing concise and informative.
• Use short, direct sentences.
• Prefer active voice.
• Focus on practical information and useful examples.
• Use bullet points when they improve readability.
• Address the reader with “you” and “your” when appropriate.
• Use facts, numbers, and examples when available.
• Avoid em dashes. Use commas or periods instead.
• Avoid clichés and generic statements.
• Avoid exaggerated marketing language.
• Avoid unnecessary adjectives and adverbs.
• Avoid repetitive sentence structures.
• Avoid unnecessary introductions and conclusions.
• Avoid filler phrases.
• Avoid excessive headings.
• Avoid excessive emojis.
• Avoid hashtags unless specifically requested.
• Avoid unnecessary markdown formatting.
• Do not repeat the same point in different words.
• Keep the tone natural and conversational.
• Write like a knowledgeable person explaining the topic to another person.
• Preserve the original meaning when rewriting.
• Do not add unsupported facts.
• Do not make the writing sound artificially casual.
• Prefer specific examples over vague claims.
• Review the final response and remove awkward, repetitive, or unnatural wording.

Before sending the response, check the writing for unnecessary repetition, generic phrases, excessive formatting, and unnatural sentence patterns.

How to Use the Prompt With ChatGPT

There are two simple ways to use it.

Use the Prompt Before Writing

If you are starting a new article, paste the instructions first.

Then give ChatGPT your actual topic.

For example:

“Write a 1,000-word article about the best AI tools for college students.”

The writing rules will guide the response.

This approach works well for:

  • Blog posts
  • LinkedIn posts
  • Newsletters
  • Product descriptions
  • Tutorials
  • Social media content
  • Marketing copy

You can also add your target audience to the request.

For example:

“Write for college students who are new to AI. Explain technical terms in simple language and use practical examples.”

The more information you provide, the easier it is to get a useful first draft.

Use the Prompt to Rewrite Existing AI Content

You do not have to start from scratch.

If you already have an AI-generated article, paste it into ChatGPT and ask it to rewrite the content using your preferred style.

For example:

“Rewrite the following article using the writing rules above. Keep the facts and original meaning. Remove repetitive wording and unnecessary sentences.”

Then paste your article.

This is useful when the information is good but the wording feels robotic.

You can also ask ChatGPT to preserve your headings, links, examples, and important facts.

Add Your Own Writing Sample

A prompt tells AI how you want the content written.

A writing sample shows AI how you actually write.

This is useful if you already have a blog or several published articles.

Take two or three paragraphs from your own writing and provide them to ChatGPT.

Then write:

“Use this writing sample as a reference for my sentence length, vocabulary, tone, and paragraph structure. Do not copy phrases or ideas from the sample.”

Your writing sample can show:

  • How long your sentences usually are
  • How you explain difficult topics
  • How formal your writing is
  • How you start paragraphs
  • How you use examples
  • How you speak to your readers

This is often more useful than adding dozens of rules to a prompt.

Save Your Writing Preferences in ChatGPT

If you use ChatGPT frequently, you may not want to paste the same instructions into every conversation.

ChatGPT provides customization options where you can tell the model how you prefer responses to be written.

Add your main writing preferences there.

The ChatGPT interface changes over time, so the exact menu name or location may differ from the screenshot you use.

After saving your preferences, start a new conversation and test them with a normal writing request.

Don’t Try to Make Every Sentence Sound “Human”

There is an important difference between improving AI writing and trying to make every sentence pass an AI detector.

You should focus on writing quality.

A good article should be:

  • Accurate
  • Useful
  • Clear
  • Easy to read
  • Relevant to the reader
  • Original in its information or perspective

Human writers do not follow a perfect formula.

They use different sentence lengths. They repeat words sometimes. They use simple language when simple language works.

If you force every sentence to follow the same pattern, the result can become unnatural.

READ NEXT

7 AI Skills You Need for Jobs in 2026

Learn the AI skills that can help you stay competitive in the 2026 job market.

Read article →
↗

Add Information AI Does Not Know

This is one of the easiest ways to improve AI-assisted content.

Add your own experience.

For example, suppose you are writing about AI coding tools.

Instead of publishing a generic comparison, explain what happened when you used the tools.

You could include:

  • Which tool you tested
  • What task you gave it
  • How long the task took
  • Where the tool performed well
  • Where it produced errors
  • Which tool you preferred
  • What you would recommend to beginners

This gives the article information that comes from your own experience.

Google’s current guidance also emphasizes original information, first-hand experience, clear authorship, and content created primarily to help people.

AI Humanization Is Not About Fooling Google

There is a common misunderstanding around AI humanizers.

The goal should not be to trick Google or an AI detector.

Google says its systems focus on helpful, reliable, people-first content. It also says using AI to create content for the primary purpose of manipulating search rankings violates its spam policies.

Using AI as part of your writing process is different from publishing large amounts of low-value automated content.

Use AI to help with tasks such as:

  • Brainstorming
  • Outlining
  • Rewriting
  • Explaining difficult concepts
  • Finding gaps in your draft
  • Improving readability

Then add your own research, experience, examples, and judgment.

That produces a much stronger article than simply generating a complete post and publishing it unchanged.

Before and After: A Simple Example

Here is an example of how you can edit an AI-style sentence.

Before:

“AI-powered writing tools are revolutionizing the content creation process by providing users with powerful capabilities that can significantly enhance productivity.”

After:

“AI writing tools help you create content faster.”

The second version removes unnecessary words.

Another example:

Before:

“In today’s rapidly evolving digital landscape, businesses are increasingly leveraging AI solutions to unlock new opportunities.”

After:

“Businesses are using AI to automate tasks and analyze data.”

The second version is more specific.

You do not need complicated vocabulary to explain a complicated topic.

Don’t Overdo the Editing

There is also a risk of going too far.

If you remove every longer sentence, every formal word, and every technical term, the article might lose its original meaning.

Keep terminology when it helps the reader.

For example, if you are writing about machine learning, terms such as “neural network,” “training data,” and “overfitting” are useful.

Instead of removing technical terms, explain them clearly.

Good writing is not about using the fewest words possible.

It is about using the right words.

How to Make AI Blog Posts More Useful

If you publish AI-assisted blog posts, focus on adding information readers cannot easily get from a generic answer.

Try adding:

Real Examples

Show how something works instead of explaining it only in theory.

Original Comparisons

Compare tools, methods, features, prices, or results when you have reliable information.

First-Hand Experience

Explain what you tested and what happened.

Screenshots

Show the actual interface, process, or result when it helps the reader.

Sources

Link to reliable primary sources when you make factual claims.

Clear Answers

Answer the main question early instead of making readers scroll through a long introduction.

These additions improve the article for readers and give the page more original value.

How to Edit an AI Article Before Publishing

Use this quick editing process.

Step 1: Read the Introduction

Remove anything that delays the answer.

Your first paragraph should tell readers what they will get from the article.

Step 2: Remove Repetition

If two paragraphs explain the same idea, combine them.

Step 3: Check Every Claim

AI can produce incorrect information.

Verify important facts using reliable sources.

Step 4: Add Your Own Information

Include examples, experience, screenshots, tests, or opinions where appropriate.

Step 5: Improve Sentence Flow

Read the article normally.

If a sentence feels awkward, rewrite it.

Step 6: Check the Headings

Keep headings that help readers find information.

Remove headings that exist only to make the article look longer.

Step 7: Read It Again

The final review is important.

Ask yourself:

“Would I recommend this article to someone who asked me this question?”

If the answer is no, improve the parts that are missing.

Common Mistakes When Humanizing AI Writing

Adding Random Slang

Natural writing does not mean using slang in every paragraph.

Write for your actual audience.

Removing Every Formal Word

Some formal and technical words are useful.

Do not replace accurate terminology simply because it sounds formal.

Adding Fake Personal Experiences

Never invent an experience you did not have.

If you did not test a product, do not write as if you did.

Changing Important Facts

A rewrite should not change the meaning of the original information.

Check important facts after rewriting.

Using Too Many Short Sentences

Short sentences are useful.

But an article made entirely of short sentences can feel repetitive.

Mix short and medium-length sentences.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is an AI humanizer prompt?

An AI humanizer prompt is a set of writing instructions designed to make AI-generated text clearer, less repetitive, and closer to a preferred writing style.

Does the prompt work with ChatGPT?

Yes. You can use the prompt with ChatGPT and other LLMs. Results will vary depending on the model, the original content, and the instructions you provide.

Can I use this prompt for blog posts?

Yes. It works well as a starting point for blog posts, tutorials, newsletters, social media content, and other forms of writing.

Should I use an AI humanizer tool?

You do not always need one. A detailed writing prompt followed by human editing can be enough for many projects.

How do I make ChatGPT writing sound more natural?

Give ChatGPT clear style instructions, provide a writing sample when useful, remove repetitive phrases, use specific examples, and review the final content yourself.

Does humanizing AI content guarantee Google Discover traffic?

No. There is no prompt that guarantees Google Discover traffic.

Google says Discover eligibility is automatic for indexed content that meets its policies, but eligibility does not guarantee appearance in Discover. Discover traffic can also change based on user interests and Google’s systems.

Final Takeaway

You do not need to make AI writing complicated.

Start with a clear prompt.

Tell the AI how you want the writing to sound. Give it a useful writing sample when appropriate. Then edit the result yourself.

The biggest improvement usually comes from adding information AI does not have, such as your own experience, original examples, screenshots, testing, research, and opinions.

Use AI as part of your writing process, not as a replacement for your judgment.

That is the difference between publishing another generic AI article and creating something readers actually find useful.
