AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year Syllabus 2026-27

The AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year Syllabus 2026-27 represents the final stage of the undergraduate engineering curriculum.

By the fourth year, students usually move beyond the core foundation subjects and focus more heavily on:

  • Advanced branch-specific subjects
  • Departmental electives
  • Open electives
  • Project work
  • Seminar or presentation components
  • Practical and application-based learning
  • Industry-oriented topics
  • Final-semester academic requirements

Because the fourth year directly connects academic learning with placements, projects, internships, and higher studies, students should follow the correct syllabus carefully.

The syllabus links on this page can help students identify the exact subjects, units, practical requirements, and academic structure applicable to their branch.

Why the AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year Syllabus Is Important

The final year of B.Tech is academically important because students are expected to apply the concepts they have learned during the earlier years of the programme.

Using the AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year Syllabus helps students:

  1. Understand the complete final-year course structure.
  2. Identify advanced technical subjects.
  3. Verify subject codes and elective papers.
  4. Plan preparation for seventh and eighth semester examinations.
  5. Organize project and seminar work.
  6. Match Notes and PYQs with the correct syllabus.
  7. Avoid preparing outdated or irrelevant topics.
  8. Balance academic preparation with placement and project activities.

A clear syllabus-based study plan can save a lot of time during the final year.

Branch-Wise AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year Syllabus

AKTU offers several B.Tech branches, and the fourth-year syllabus varies significantly depending on the engineering discipline.

Students should select the syllabus for their own branch instead of relying on similar subject names.

Depending on the branch, the fourth-year curriculum may include:

  • Advanced core subjects
  • Professional electives
  • Open electives
  • Specialized laboratories
  • Major project work
  • Seminar activities
  • Research-oriented topics
  • Industry-relevant subjects
  • Technical or professional skill courses

After opening a syllabus PDF, always verify:

  • Branch name
  • Semester
  • Subject title
  • Subject code
  • Applicable course structure

This helps ensure that you are preparing from the correct curriculum.

What You Can Find in the Fourth Year Syllabus PDF

The syllabus PDF may include detailed academic information such as:

  • Subject code
  • Subject name
  • Number of credits
  • Lecture hours
  • Practical hours
  • Tutorial requirements
  • Unit-wise topics
  • Course objectives
  • Course outcomes
  • Suggested textbooks
  • Reference books
  • Laboratory components
  • Project requirements
  • Elective subjects
  • Assessment structure

Students can use this information to organize their study plan more effectively.

Advanced Technical Subjects in Fourth Year

The fourth year usually contains more specialized technical subjects than the earlier years.

The exact subjects depend on the student’s branch and elective selection.

For example, final-year students may study advanced topics related to:

  • Artificial Intelligence
  • Machine Learning
  • Data Science
  • Cyber Security
  • Communication Systems
  • Embedded Systems
  • VLSI
  • Power Systems
  • Structural Engineering
  • Manufacturing
  • Thermal Engineering
  • Industrial Processes
  • Biotechnology Applications
  • Automation
  • Cloud or Distributed Systems

The actual subject list depends entirely on the applicable branch and curriculum.

Students should use the syllabus as the primary reference before downloading Notes or PYQs.

Open Electives in AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year

The fourth-year curriculum may include multiple open elective papers across the seventh and eighth semesters.

For this syllabus page, the dedicated entries for:

  • VII Semester: Open Elective-II
  • VIII Semester: Open Electives-III & IV

are provided at the end of the syllabus table.

Students should check which elective has actually been selected, allotted, or prescribed for their branch before downloading the relevant syllabus.

Before preparing an elective, verify:

  • Elective title
  • Subject code
  • Semester
  • Branch eligibility
  • Applicable course structure

Do not prepare every elective listed in the university curriculum.

VII Semester: Open Elective-II

The seventh semester may include Open Elective-II, depending on the applicable B.Tech curriculum.

Open electives allow students to study a subject beyond the narrow scope of their core branch.

The exact subject available to a student may depend on:

  • University curriculum
  • College offering
  • Branch eligibility
  • Student selection
  • Applicable subject code

The VII Semester: Open Elective-II syllabus link is listed at the end of the syllabus table on this page.

VIII Semester: Open Electives-III & IV

The eighth semester may include Open Electives-III & IV.

These electives can help students explore specialized, interdisciplinary, or industry-oriented topics during the final semester.

Students should check the exact elective assigned or selected before preparing from Notes or PYQs.

The VIII Semester: Open Electives-III & IV syllabus links are provided at the end of the syllabus table after the branch-wise entries.

Major Project in B.Tech Fourth Year

The major project is one of the most important components of the final year.

Depending on the branch and curriculum, students may be required to:

  • Select a project topic
  • Form a project group
  • Prepare a proposal
  • Conduct research or development work
  • Implement the project
  • Prepare documentation
  • Give presentations
  • Appear for project evaluation
  • Attend viva or project defense

Students should check the syllabus and departmental guidelines for the exact project requirements.

A good project can also be useful during:

  • Placement interviews
  • Internship applications
  • Higher studies
  • Resume building
  • Technical portfolio development

Seminar and Presentation Components

Some branches may include seminar or presentation-based academic components.

These may require students to:

  • Select a technical topic
  • Prepare a report
  • Create a presentation
  • Explain the topic before faculty
  • Answer viva questions

Students should follow the syllabus and college instructions regarding topic selection, report format, and evaluation criteria.

How to Download AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year Syllabus PDF

Follow these steps to download the syllabus:

  1. Find your B.Tech branch in the syllabus table.
  2. Click the relevant Download PDF button.
  3. Open the syllabus document.
  4. Verify the branch and subject codes.
  5. Save the PDF on your phone, laptop, or Google Drive.
  6. Scroll to the end of the table for VII Semester: Open Elective-II and VIII Semester: Open Electives-III & IV.

Always check that the syllabus matches your current academic structure.

How to Use the Fourth Year Syllabus for Exam Preparation

The syllabus can be used as a complete preparation roadmap.

1. Divide subjects semester-wise

Create separate lists for:

  • 7th Semester
  • 8th Semester

Then classify subjects as:

  • Core
  • Elective
  • Practical
  • Project
  • Seminar

This makes final-year planning much easier.

2. Break every subject into units

For each theory subject, list all units and topics.

You can track your progress using:

  • Not Started
  • In Progress
  • Completed
  • Revised

This helps prevent important topics from being missed.

3. Match Notes with the syllabus

Before using any Notes PDF, compare its chapters with the official syllabus.

This helps avoid:

  • Old topics
  • Deleted units
  • Wrong subject codes
  • Irrelevant content

4. Use PYQs after completing concepts

Previous year question papers are useful for identifying:

  • Repeated questions
  • Important units
  • Common numerical problems
  • Theory patterns
  • High-weightage concepts

But PYQs should not replace complete syllabus preparation.

5. Prepare project work separately

Do not mix major project preparation with regular theory subjects.

Keep separate folders for:

  • Project documentation
  • Source code
  • Research papers
  • Presentation
  • Viva preparation
  • Final report

AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year Study Strategy

A practical final-year strategy can follow this order:

Syllabus → Notes → Concepts → PYQs → Project Work → Revision

Students should try to balance academics with:

  • Placements
  • Internships
  • Technical skill development
  • Competitive exam preparation
  • Project work

The final year can become hectic if everything is left for the last few weeks.

A syllabus-based approach helps keep academic preparation organized.

Importance of Subject Codes

Subject codes are especially important in the final year because similar elective or advanced subject names may appear under different curricula.

Before using Notes or PYQs, verify:

  • Branch
  • Semester
  • Subject name
  • Subject code
  • Course structure

This helps prevent students from preparing the wrong subject.

Using Notes and PYQs with the Fourth Year Syllabus

The AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year Syllabus should act as the central reference for all study material.

For each subject:

  1. Open the syllabus.
  2. Check every unit.
  3. Match your Notes to the syllabus.
  4. Solve relevant PYQs.
  5. Identify frequently repeated topics.
  6. Revise uncovered topics separately.

This gives a more balanced preparation strategy.

Final Year Preparation for Placements

The fourth year is not only about semester examinations.

Students may also need to prepare for:

  • Campus placements
  • Off-campus jobs
  • Internships
  • Coding interviews
  • Technical interviews
  • Aptitude tests
  • Group discussions
  • HR interviews

It is useful to manage academic and placement preparation together.

For example:

  • Complete syllabus topics regularly.
  • Practice technical questions related to core subjects.
  • Keep project concepts clear.
  • Revise important third-year and fourth-year subjects for interviews.

Final Year Project and Resume Preparation

Students should also use their project work to strengthen their resume.

A good final-year project entry should clearly mention:

  • Project title
  • Problem statement
  • Technologies used
  • Your contribution
  • Key features
  • Final outcome

Students should understand their project deeply because interviewers often ask detailed technical questions about it.

Common Mistakes Students Should Avoid

Using the wrong syllabus

Always confirm the branch and subject code before preparation.

Ignoring electives

Elective subjects are part of the curriculum and should be prepared according to the selected paper.

Depending only on PYQs

Previous year papers are important, but they do not cover every possible syllabus topic.

Ignoring the elective entries at the end of the table

Students should remember to check the VII Semester: Open Elective-II and VIII Semester: Open Electives-III & IV entries provided at the end of the syllabus table.

Ignoring project work until the end

Major projects require planning, implementation, documentation, and presentation. Start early.

Using outdated Notes

Older Notes may still be useful, but compare them with the current syllabus before studying.

Neglecting semester subjects because of placements

Placement preparation is important, but academic performance should not be ignored.

Benefits of Saving the Syllabus Offline

Keeping a local copy of the syllabus can help throughout the final year.

Students can quickly:

  • Check subject codes
  • Verify units
  • Compare Notes
  • Match PYQs
  • Plan revision
  • Track electives
  • Organize project work

A useful folder structure can be:

Fourth Year

  • Syllabus
  • Notes
  • PYQs
  • Assignments
  • Practical
  • Project
  • Seminar

This keeps all academic material organized.

How to Plan Seventh Semester Preparation

The seventh semester often contains a combination of advanced subjects, electives, practical work, and project-related activities.

Students can:

  1. Complete theory units regularly.
  2. Prepare practical work alongside classes.
  3. Start project planning early.
  4. Solve PYQs after each unit.
  5. Revise important technical concepts for placements.
  6. Check the applicable Open Elective-II syllabus from the end of the table.

How to Plan Eighth Semester Preparation

The eighth semester may have comparatively fewer theory subjects in some branches, but project work can become more intensive.

Students should focus on:

  • Remaining theory subjects
  • Open Electives-III & IV where applicable
  • Project completion
  • Final report
  • Presentation
  • Viva
  • Placement preparation
  • Pending academic requirements

Always check the applicable syllabus because the exact structure varies by branch.

Final Words

The AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year Syllabus provides a complete roadmap for final-year students preparing for advanced subjects, electives, projects, practical work, and semester examinations.

Students should use the branch-wise syllabus links on this page to verify their subject codes and course structure before downloading Notes, PYQs, or other study material. After reviewing your branch syllabus, remember that the dedicated syllabus entries for VII Semester: Open Elective-II and VIII Semester: Open Electives-III & IV are available at the end of the syllabus table.

A well-organized final-year preparation strategy should combine syllabus-based study, previous year papers, project work, practical preparation, and placement readiness.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year Syllabus?

The AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year Syllabus contains the branch-wise subjects, advanced technical courses, electives, project components, practical requirements, and academic structure prescribed for final-year B.Tech students.

Where can I download the AKTU B.Tech Fourth Year Syllabus PDF?

You can download the relevant branch syllabus using the Download PDF button provided in the syllabus table on this page.

Where is the VII Semester Open Elective-II syllabus available?

The VII Semester: Open Elective-II syllabus is listed at the end of the syllabus table on this page.

Where are the VIII Semester Open Electives-III & IV listed?

The VIII Semester: Open Electives-III & IV syllabus entries are provided at the end of the syllabus table, after the branch-wise syllabus entries.

Is the fourth-year syllabus the same for every B.Tech branch?

No. Final-year subjects vary significantly according to the engineering branch, electives, and applicable course structure.

Does AKTU B.Tech fourth year include elective subjects?

Yes. Depending on the applicable curriculum, students may have professional, departmental, or open electives across the seventh and eighth semesters.

Is there a major project in B.Tech fourth year?

Most B.Tech programmes include a major project or similar project-based academic component in the final year. Students should check their branch syllabus for the exact requirements.

Should I verify subject codes before downloading Notes or PYQs?

Yes. Subject codes should always be checked because similar subject names may appear under different branches or curriculum structures.

Can I prepare only from previous year papers?

No. PYQs are helpful for understanding the question pattern, but students should prepare the complete syllabus.

How should I balance placements and semester preparation?

Follow a regular study schedule for semester subjects while keeping separate time for placement preparation, technical skills, aptitude, project work, and interview practice.

AKTU B.Tech Third Year Syllabus 2026-27

The AKTU B.Tech Third Year Syllabus 2026-27 is an important academic reference for students entering the advanced stage of their undergraduate engineering programme.

By the third year, most branches shift heavily toward specialized technical subjects, laboratories, elective courses, design-oriented topics, and application-based learning. Because of this, students should rely on the correct syllabus before preparing Notes, PYQs, assignments, practical files, or semester exam material.

On this page, students can access branch-wise syllabus PDFs and review the academic structure applicable to their course.

The syllabus may include information such as:

  • Core technical subjects
  • Department-specific courses
  • Subject codes
  • Unit-wise topics
  • Theory and practical components
  • Open electives
  • Laboratory courses
  • Project-related components
  • Common non-credit courses
  • Course outcomes and learning objectives

Students should always confirm their branch, semester, and subject code before using any syllabus PDF.

Why the AKTU B.Tech Third Year Syllabus Is Important

The third year of B.Tech is academically significant because students begin studying more advanced subjects directly related to their engineering discipline.

Using the AKTU B.Tech Third Year Syllabus can help students:

  1. Understand the complete course structure.
  2. Identify the units prescribed for each subject.
  3. Match Notes and study materials with the correct topics.
  4. Plan preparation for internal and end-semester examinations.
  5. Identify branch-specific electives and practical subjects.
  6. Avoid studying outdated or irrelevant topics.
  7. Organize preparation according to subject credits and difficulty.
  8. Check the correct syllabus before solving previous year papers.

A syllabus-based study plan is generally more efficient than preparing randomly from different resources.

Branch-Wise AKTU B.Tech Third Year Syllabus

The third-year syllabus differs considerably across engineering branches.

Students should therefore select the syllabus corresponding to their own branch rather than relying only on similar subject names.

Depending on the programme, the third-year curriculum may contain:

  • Advanced core subjects
  • Departmental electives
  • Open electives
  • Laboratory work
  • Professional or technical courses
  • Seminar or project-related components
  • Non-credit courses

After opening a syllabus PDF, verify the branch name, subject codes, semester, and applicable course structure.

What You Can Find in the Third Year Syllabus PDF

The syllabus PDF may provide detailed academic information including:

  • Subject title
  • Subject code
  • Credit structure
  • Lecture hours
  • Tutorial hours
  • Practical hours
  • Unit-wise syllabus
  • Course objectives
  • Course outcomes
  • Recommended books
  • Reference materials
  • Laboratory experiments
  • Elective details

These details help students understand what needs to be studied and how the subject is evaluated during the semester.

Third Year Core Subjects

Third-year core subjects are usually more specialized than the subjects studied during the first and second years.

The exact subjects depend on the student’s engineering branch.

For example, different branches may focus on areas such as:

  • Computer systems and software
  • Electronics and communication systems
  • Mechanical design and manufacturing
  • Civil engineering structures
  • Electrical systems
  • Chemical processes
  • Biotechnology applications
  • Data-oriented technologies
  • Industrial applications

Students should not assume that subjects are identical across branches even when similar terminology is used.

Always verify the syllabus PDF and subject code.

Open Elective-1 of 6th Semester

The third-year curriculum may include Open Elective-1 in the 6th Semester.

Open electives allow students to study selected subjects beyond the narrow scope of their primary engineering branch.

The exact elective available to a student may depend on:

  • University curriculum
  • College offering
  • Branch eligibility
  • Student selection
  • Seat availability
  • Applicable subject code

The syllabus for Open Elective-1 of 6th Sem is provided separately at the end of the syllabus table on this page.

Students should check which elective has actually been allotted or selected before downloading the syllabus.

Common Non-Credit Courses

The curriculum may also include Common Non-Credit Courses.

These courses may form part of the academic structure without carrying the same credit weight as regular technical subjects.

Even if a course is non-credit, students should still check the prescribed syllabus and university requirements.

The Common Non-Credit Courses syllabus is provided at the end of the syllabus table, after the branch-wise syllabus entries.

Students should verify whether a particular non-credit course applies to their branch, semester, or academic session.

How to Download AKTU B.Tech Third Year Syllabus PDF

Follow these steps to access your syllabus:

  1. Find your engineering branch in the syllabus table.
  2. Click the relevant Download PDF button.
  3. Open the syllabus document.
  4. Verify your branch and subject codes.
  5. Save the PDF for offline reference.
  6. Check the end of the table for Open Elective-1 of 6th Sem and Common Non-Credit Courses, if applicable.

Always use the syllabus that matches your current course structure.

How to Use the Syllabus for Semester Preparation

Downloading the syllabus is useful only when it is actively used during preparation.

1. Divide each subject into units

Write down all units for each subject and create a simple progress tracker.

You can mark topics as:

  • Not Started
  • In Progress
  • Completed
  • Revised

This makes it easier to manage multiple technical subjects.

2. Match Notes with the syllabus

Before relying on Notes, compare their chapter coverage with the prescribed syllabus.

This helps you avoid:

  • Missing important topics
  • Studying deleted topics
  • Using content from an older syllabus
  • Preparing irrelevant units

3. Use PYQs after understanding the syllabus

Previous year question papers are highly useful for identifying:

  • Repeated concepts
  • Important numerical problems
  • Frequently asked theories
  • High-weightage units
  • Common question patterns

However, PYQs should not replace the complete syllabus.

4. Separate theory and practical preparation

Third-year students often have several laboratory and application-based subjects.

For practical courses, prepare:

  • Experiments
  • Viva questions
  • Practical files
  • Procedures
  • Relevant theory
  • Observations and results

5. Revise with a syllabus checklist

Before semester examinations, compare your preparation against the syllabus once again.

This helps identify topics that may have been missed during regular study.

AKTU B.Tech Third Year Exam Preparation Strategy

A good third-year preparation strategy should combine multiple resources in the correct order.

A practical sequence is:

Syllabus → Notes → Concepts → PYQs → Practice → Revision

Start by checking the complete syllabus.

Then:

  1. Study each unit systematically.
  2. Make short revision notes.
  3. Practice numerical and application-based questions.
  4. Solve previous year papers.
  5. Identify weak units.
  6. Revise those units again.
  7. Use the syllabus as a final checklist.

This approach is especially useful for technical subjects where understanding concepts is more important than memorizing isolated answers.

Importance of Subject Codes

Students should always verify subject codes before preparing from any resource.

Similar subject names may appear in:

  • Different branches
  • Different course structures
  • Different semesters
  • Revised university schemes

A Notes PDF or PYQ may look relevant but still belong to another subject code.

Before studying, confirm:

  • Branch
  • Semester
  • Subject name
  • Subject code
  • Academic structure

This simple check can prevent a lot of unnecessary confusion.

Third Year Electives and Specialized Subjects

The third year often introduces more flexibility into the curriculum through specialized and elective subjects.

Students may encounter:

  • Departmental electives
  • Open electives
  • Advanced technical subjects
  • Interdisciplinary courses

Electives should be selected and prepared according to the subject officially assigned or chosen.

Do not prepare every elective listed in the university syllabus.

Check your selected subject first.

Using Notes and PYQs with the Third Year Syllabus

The AKTU B.Tech Third Year Syllabus should act as the central reference when using Notes and previous year question papers.

For every subject:

  1. Open the syllabus.
  2. Check the unit structure.
  3. Match available Notes with those units.
  4. Solve relevant PYQs.
  5. Mark frequently repeated topics.
  6. Revise uncovered syllabus topics separately.

This makes your preparation more balanced.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Using the wrong branch syllabus

Always confirm your engineering branch before downloading.

Ignoring subject codes

A similar title does not always mean the same subject.

Studying only from previous year papers

PYQs help with pattern analysis, but they do not cover every possible syllabus topic.

Forgetting Open Electives

If you have an open elective in the 6th semester, check the corresponding syllabus listed at the end of the table.

Ignoring Common Non-Credit Courses

Non-credit does not necessarily mean optional. Check the university and college requirements.

Using old Notes without verification

Older Notes can still be useful, but compare them with the current syllabus before preparation.

Benefits of Saving the Syllabus Offline

Keeping a local copy of your syllabus can help throughout the academic year.

You can quickly:

  • Verify topics during classes
  • Match Notes with syllabus units
  • Check subject codes
  • Prepare for sessional exams
  • Organize practical files
  • Revise before end-semester exams
  • Compare previous year papers with the curriculum

Students can create separate folders for each subject containing:

  • Syllabus
  • Notes
  • PYQs
  • Assignments
  • Practical material

This keeps preparation organized.

Final Words

The AKTU B.Tech Third Year Syllabus provides a clear roadmap for students studying advanced branch-specific subjects in the third year of B.Tech. Use the branch-wise syllabus table to access the correct curriculum, verify subject codes, and plan preparation according to the prescribed units.

After checking your branch syllabus, remember to review the entries at the end of the syllabus table for Open Elective-1 of 6th Sem and Common Non-Credit Courses. Using the syllabus together with reliable Notes, PYQs, textbooks, and practical material can make third-year preparation much more systematic and effective.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the AKTU B.Tech Third Year Syllabus?

The AKTU B.Tech Third Year Syllabus contains the branch-specific subjects, course structure, unit-wise topics, electives, practical components, and other academic details prescribed for third-year B.Tech students.

Where can I download the AKTU B.Tech Third Year Syllabus PDF?

You can download the relevant syllabus using the branch-wise Download PDF links provided in the syllabus table on this page.

Is the third-year syllabus the same for all B.Tech branches?

No. Third-year subjects vary significantly according to the engineering branch. Students should use only the syllabus applicable to their branch and subject codes.

Where is the Open Elective-1 of 6th Sem syllabus available?

The Open Elective-1 of 6th Sem syllabus is provided at the end of the syllabus table on this page.

Where can I find the Common Non-Credit Courses syllabus?

The Common Non-Credit Courses syllabus is also provided at the end of the syllabus table, after the branch-wise syllabus entries.

Should I verify subject codes before preparing?

Yes. Subject-code verification is important because similar subject names may appear under different branches, semesters, or course structures.

Can I prepare only from PYQs?

No. Previous year papers are useful for understanding question patterns, but students should prepare the complete syllabus before depending on PYQs.

How should I use the third-year syllabus for preparation?

Divide every subject unit-wise, study from reliable Notes and textbooks, solve PYQs after completing the concepts, and use the syllabus as a final revision checklist.

Are open electives compulsory for every student?

The applicable elective structure depends on the university curriculum, branch, semester, and college offering. Students should check the elective assigned or selected for their course.

Are Common Non-Credit Courses unimportant because they carry no credit?

No. Students should still check the applicable university and college requirements. A non-credit course may still involve attendance, assessment, completion, or other academic requirements.

The second year of B.Tech is an important stage because students begin studying subjects directly related to their engineering branch.

  • Mathematics-V

A syllabus-based approach is especially useful for Mathematics because it helps students identify exactly which numerical methods, transforms, probability topics, differential equations, or other mathematical concepts are included in their paper.

Technical Communication

Technical Communication is another course that may appear in the second-year curriculum.

The subject generally focuses on communication and professional skills relevant to engineering students. Students preparing for this paper should follow the prescribed syllabus because the topics can be divided into several communication-related areas and assessment components.

Create a list of all units and topics for each subject.

  • In progress
  • Completed
  • Revised

While solving PYQs, identify:

  • Frequently repeated topics
  • Important units
  • Common numerical problems
  • Theory questions
  • Topics that have appeared in multiple examinations

Do not completely skip a syllabus topic simply because it has not appeared recently in previous papers.

Check:

  • Experiments
  • Viva topics
  • Practical files
  • Lab concepts
  • Related theory

Syllabus → Notes → Important Topics → PYQs → Revision

Start by understanding the complete syllabus. Then collect notes according to each unit. Once the concepts are clear, solve previous year question papers and identify important recurring areas.

This approach makes preparation more focused and reduces unnecessary workload.

Before preparing any subject, verify:

  • Branch
  • Semester
  • Subject name
  • Subject code
  • Applicable syllabus or curriculum

If the subject code does not match, check the appropriate syllabus before continuing your preparation.

  • Faculty-provided material

  • Previous year question papers

  • Practice questions

Should I check the subject code before downloading the syllabus?

Yes. Always verify the subject code along with the subject name, branch, and semester. This helps ensure that you are using the correct syllabus for your course structure.

How should I prepare using the AKTU B.Tech Second Year Syllabus?

Start by dividing each subject into units, study the topics using reliable Notes or textbooks, solve previous year papers after completing the syllabus, and use the syllabus again as a checklist during revision.

Does the syllabus include open electives?

The AKTU B.Tech First Year Syllabus is an important academic reference for students beginning their B.Tech programme at Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University. It helps students understand the curriculum applicable to the first year and identify the correct syllabus according to their engineering stream.

For the 2026-27 academic session, students should first check the stream-wise classification of their branch before opening the syllabus link. This page provides the AKTU B.Tech First Year Syllabus PDF links in one place, along with the stream classification needed to choose the correct syllabus.

The table is organised stream-wise so that students can quickly find the syllabus relevant to Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Science & Engineering, Textile Engineering, Biotechnology, Chemical Engineering and Agricultural Engineering.

AKTU B.Tech First Year Stream-Wise Branch Classification

Before downloading the syllabus, check which AKTU stream your branch belongs to. The university’s stream-wise classification groups the branches as follows.

1. Civil Engineering Stream (CE)

The Civil Engineering Stream (CE) includes:

  • Civil Engineering
  • Environmental Engineering

Students enrolled in either of these branches should refer to the syllabus provided for the Civil Engineering stream.

2. Mechanical Engineering Stream (ME)

The Mechanical Engineering Stream (ME) covers several mechanical and production-oriented branches:

  • Mechanical Engineering
  • Automobile Engineering
  • Aeronautical Engineering
  • Industrial Production Engineering
  • Manufacturing Technology
  • Mining Engineering

If your branch is listed above, use the syllabus available under the Mechanical Engineering stream.

3. Electrical Engineering Stream (EE)

The Electrical Engineering Stream (EE) includes:

  • Electrical Engineering
  • Electrical & Electronics Engineering
  • Electrical & Computer Engineering

Students from these branches fall under the common Electrical Engineering stream for the purpose of this classification.

4. Electronics Engineering Stream (ECE)

The Electronics Engineering Stream (ECE) has the widest group of electronics and communication-related branches. It includes:

  • Electronics Engineering
  • Electronics and Communication Engineering
  • Electronics and Communication (Advanced Communication Technology)
  • Electronics Engineering (VLSI Design and Technology)
  • Electronics and Instrumentation Engineering
  • Electronics, Instrumentation and Control Engineering
  • Electronics and Computer Engineering

Students studying any of these programmes should check the syllabus listed for the Electronics Engineering stream.

5. Computer Science & Engineering Stream (CSE)

The Computer Science & Engineering Stream (CSE) includes the core CSE programme as well as several specialised computing branches:

  • Computer Science and Engineering
  • Computer Science
  • Computer Engineering
  • Information Technology
  • Computer Science and Information Technology
  • Computer Science & Technology
  • Computer Science and Design
  • Computer Science Engineering (Hindi)
  • Computer Science and Engineering (Artificial Intelligence)
  • Computer Science and Engineering (Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning)
  • Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
  • Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Data Science
  • Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)
  • Computer Science & Engineering (Cyber Security)
  • Computer Science and Engineering (Internet of Things)
  • Cyber Security
  • Data Science

If you are studying one of these programmes, the B.Tech First Year Syllabus AKTU listed under the CSE stream is the relevant syllabus category to check.

6. Textile Engineering Stream (TE)

The Textile Engineering Stream (TE) includes:

  • Textile Technology
  • Handloom & Textile Technology
  • Carpet & Textile Technology

Students from these programmes should use the Textile Engineering stream syllabus.

7. Biotechnology Stream (BT)

The Biotechnology Stream (BT) covers:

  • Biotechnology
  • Biomedical Engineering
  • Bioinformatics

These branches are grouped under the Biotechnology stream.

8. Chemical Engineering Stream (CH)

The Chemical Engineering Stream (CH) includes:

  • Chemical Engineering
  • Plastic Engineering
  • Food Technology

Students enrolled in these branches should refer to the syllabus provided for the Chemical Engineering stream.

9. Agricultural Engineering Stream (AG)

The Agricultural Engineering Stream (AG) includes:

  • Agricultural Engineering

Students of Agricultural Engineering should use the syllabus listed under the Agricultural Engineering stream.

Which AKTU First Year Syllabus Should You Download?

The branch name mentioned on your admission or university records may not always be identical to the stream name used in the syllabus table.

For example, a student enrolled in Computer Science and Engineering (Artificial Intelligence) falls under the Computer Science & Engineering Stream, while a student of Automobile Engineering falls under the Mechanical Engineering Stream.

So, before using the download links below:

  1. Find your exact branch in the stream classification above.
  2. Note the corresponding stream.
  3. Locate that stream in the syllabus download table.
  4. Open the available syllabus PDF.
  5. Keep the syllabus saved for subject planning and semester-wise study preparation.

This stream mapping is especially useful for specialised branches because several programmes share a common first-year academic structure.

About the AKTU B.Tech First Year Syllabus 2026-27

The AKTU B.Tech First Year Syllabus serves as a roadmap for understanding the academic curriculum during the first year of B.Tech. Instead of studying topics randomly, students can use the syllabus to identify what is actually included in their course and plan their preparation accordingly.

Keeping a copy of the syllabus is useful throughout the academic session because it can help you:

  • understand the overall course structure;
  • identify the topics that need to be covered;
  • organise study material according to the curriculum;
  • compare your classroom progress with the prescribed syllabus;
  • plan revision before university examinations;
  • avoid spending unnecessary time on topics outside the applicable curriculum.

The syllabus should be treated as the starting point when organising notes, books and other study resources.

How to Use the AKTU Syllabus for Study Planning

Downloading the syllabus is useful only when you actually use it while studying.

Start by reviewing the curriculum and creating a simple checklist of the topics you need to complete. As classes progress, mark the portions that have already been covered and keep track of the remaining topics.

You can also organise your study resources according to the syllabus. Keep your notes, previous year questions and other material mapped to the relevant topics rather than collecting resources without knowing where they fit in the curriculum.

Before examinations, revisit the syllabus and compare it with your completed notes. This makes it easier to identify topics that may still require revision.

Why the Correct Stream Matters

AKTU offers B.Tech programmes under many traditional and specialised branch names. Because related branches can be grouped into a common stream, searching only by the exact branch name may sometimes create confusion.

For example:

  • Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning programmes are included within the CSE stream classification.
  • Automobile Engineering is included within the Mechanical Engineering stream.
  • Electrical & Electronics Engineering is included within the Electrical Engineering stream.
  • Biomedical Engineering and Bioinformatics are included within the Biotechnology stream.
  • Food Technology is included within the Chemical Engineering stream.

Checking the stream first therefore reduces the chance of opening the wrong syllabus.

Keep the Academic Session in Mind

This page is organised for students looking for the AKTU Syllabus 2026-27. When using any syllabus document, make sure it corresponds to the curriculum applicable to your admission batch and academic session.

University curricula can change over time, so students should avoid relying only on old PDFs saved from previous batches when a more relevant syllabus is available.

The canonical page URL remains the same so that updated syllabus information can be maintained without requiring students to search for a completely different page every academic session.

AKTU B.Tech Syllabus and Related Study Material

Once you know the correct syllabus, the next step is to organise your preparation around it. Syllabus, notes and previous year questions serve different purposes but work best when used together.

The syllabus tells you what needs to be studied. Notes help you understand and revise the topics, while previous year questions can help you understand the type of questions that have appeared in university examinations.

Which stream does Automobile Engineering come under?

Automobile Engineering is listed under the Mechanical Engineering Stream (ME) along with Mechanical Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Industrial Production Engineering, Manufacturing Technology and Mining Engineering.

Which syllabus should an Electrical & Electronics Engineering student use?

Electrical & Electronics Engineering is grouped under the Electrical Engineering Stream (EE) in the stream-wise classification.

Is the AKTU syllabus useful for exam preparation?

Yes. The syllabus helps students identify the curriculum they are expected to study. It can be used as a checklist while organising notes, covering topics and planning revision before examinations.

title.rendered: AKTU Makes ABC ID Mandatory for All Students; Update on ERP Before 15 August 2026

content.rendered:
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow has issued an important notification directing all affiliated colleges and students to ensure that the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) ID is created and updated on the university ERP portal. The instruction applies to both existing students and those taking admission in the 2026–27 academic session. According to the university, the ABC ID must be updated on or before 15 August 2026.

The university stated that this initiative is being implemented in accordance with the Government of India’s Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) framework under the National Education Policy (NEP). The objective is to digitally maintain students’ academic records and facilitate secure credit storage and verification.

Why is the ABC ID Important?

AKTU has clarified that students’ examination results are being uploaded to NAD DigiLocker. If a student’s ABC ID is not available or updated on the university ERP portal, their examination records cannot be properly synchronized with NAD DigiLocker. This may create difficulties in maintaining official academic records.

The university has therefore instructed all students to complete the process within the prescribed deadline.

Who Needs to Update the ABC ID?

The notification is applicable to:

  • Students currently studying in AKTU-affiliated colleges.
  • Newly admitted students for the 2026–27 academic session.
  • Students whose ABC ID has not yet been linked with the AKTU ERP portal.

Last Date

Students must complete the ABC ID update process before 15 August 2026 by logging into the AKTU ERP portal and entering their Academic Bank of Credits ID.

What Happens If You Don’t Update It?

The university has warned that if the ABC ID is not updated within the prescribed timeline:

  • Examination data may not be reflected correctly on the university ERP.
  • Results may not be uploaded or updated on NAD DigiLocker.
  • Academic records may remain incomplete until the required information is submitted.

How Students Can Complete the Process

Students who have already generated an ABC ID should simply log in to the AKTU ERP portal and verify that their ID has been updated successfully. Those who have not yet created an ABC ID should generate one first and then link it with their university ERP account before the deadline.

In case of any technical issue, students should immediately contact their respective college administration for assistance.

Instructions for Colleges

AKTU has also directed principals and affiliated institutions to ensure that every eligible student completes the ABC ID update process. Colleges have been asked to monitor compliance so that students do not face issues related to examination records and academic data management.

Official Notice at a Glance

Conclusion

Students studying in AKTU-affiliated colleges should treat this notification as a priority. Updating the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) ID before 15 August 2026 will help ensure that examination records and results are properly maintained on the university ERP and NAD DigiLocker. Students are advised to complete the process as early as possible to avoid last-minute issues.

title.rendered: Dexcom Recruitment 2026: Software Development Engineer 2 Hiring in Bengaluru – Apply Online

content.rendered:
Dexcom, one of the world’s leading healthcare technology companies, has officially announced its Recruitment Drive 2026 for the position of Software Development Engineer 2 (SDE 2) in Bengaluru, Karnataka. This hiring opportunity is ideal for software engineers with 2 to 5 years of professional experience who want to work on cutting-edge cloud technologies while building healthcare solutions that positively impact millions of lives across the globe.

If you are passionate about software development, cloud computing, scalable systems, and modern web technologies, this is an excellent opportunity to join a globally recognized organization that values innovation, continuous learning, and engineering excellence.

About Dexcom

Dexcom Corporation (NASDAQ: DXCM) is a global pioneer in Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) technology. Founded more than 25 years ago, the company transformed diabetes management through advanced biosensing technologies that provide real-time glucose insights to patients and healthcare professionals.

Today, Dexcom continues expanding beyond diabetes management by developing intelligent healthcare platforms that deliver personalized health insights and improve patient outcomes worldwide. With operations across multiple countries, the company serves millions of users while maintaining the highest standards of quality, security, and innovation.

Job Overview

About the Role

The selected candidates will become part of Dexcom’s rapidly growing engineering team in Bengaluru. Engineers will contribute to the development of Dexcom Clarity, a cloud-based healthcare analytics platform that helps healthcare professionals analyze Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) data and make informed treatment decisions.

The role involves working with highly skilled engineers located across India and the United States while contributing throughout the complete software development lifecycle. Candidates will design scalable software systems, build cloud-native applications, participate in code reviews, and develop secure software that complies with healthcare industry standards.

This position offers exposure to modern engineering practices, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, Agile development, and large-scale healthcare applications.

Key Responsibilities

The Software Development Engineer 2 will be responsible for:

  • Designing, developing, testing, and maintaining scalable software applications.
  • Developing high-quality frontend and backend services.
  • Writing clean, efficient, maintainable, and well-documented code.
  • Collaborating with product managers, designers, quality engineers, and global engineering teams.
  • Participating in code reviews and following engineering best practices.
  • Troubleshooting production issues and improving application performance.
  • Building secure software while complying with privacy and healthcare regulations.
  • Working with Agile methodologies including sprint planning and estimation.
  • Continuously learning new technologies and contributing to team knowledge sharing.

Eligibility Criteria

To apply for this position, candidates should possess:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Professional software development experience ranging from 2 to 5 years.
  • Strong knowledge of algorithms, object-oriented programming, and data structures.
  • Experience developing web applications or backend services.
  • Good analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong communication and teamwork abilities.
  • Willingness to work with globally distributed engineering teams.

Required Technical Skills

Candidates should have experience with one or more of the following technologies:

  • Java
  • JavaScript
  • TypeScript
  • Node.js
  • Go
  • Scala
  • Ruby
  • REST APIs
  • Software Design Principles
  • Data Structures & Algorithms
  • Version Control Systems (Git)

Preferred Skills

Having experience with the following technologies will be an added advantage:

  • React.js
  • Svelte
  • Ember.js
  • Amazon Web Services (AWS)
  • Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
  • Docker
  • Kubernetes
  • CI/CD Pipelines
  • Monitoring & Observability Tools
  • Healthcare Software Development
  • Data-Intensive Applications

Why You Should Join Dexcom

Dexcom offers much more than just a software engineering role. Employees get an opportunity to work on products that directly improve people’s health and quality of life.

Some major benefits include:

  • Opportunity to work on life-changing healthcare technology.
  • Competitive salary package.
  • Global exposure through collaboration with international engineering teams.
  • Comprehensive employee benefits program.
  • Continuous learning and internal training programs.
  • Tuition reimbursement for higher education.
  • Career growth opportunities across global offices.
  • Modern engineering culture focused on innovation and ownership.
  • Exposure to cloud-native architectures and large-scale distributed systems.

Expected Salary

Dexcom has not officially disclosed the salary package for this role. However, based on industry trends and previous compensation data, candidates can expect a package ranging between:

₹18 LPA to ₹35 LPA

The final compensation depends upon the candidate’s experience, technical expertise, interview performance, and overall profile. Additional benefits may include performance bonuses, employee wellness programs, insurance coverage, and stock-related benefits.

Selection Process

The recruitment process generally consists of the following stages:

  1. Online Application Submission
  2. Resume Shortlisting
  3. Online Technical Assessment (if applicable)
  4. Technical Interview Round
  5. System Design or Coding Interview
  6. Hiring Manager Discussion
  7. HR Interview
  8. Final Offer Letter

Candidates with strong problem-solving abilities, solid programming fundamentals, and practical development experience will have a better chance of getting shortlisted.

How to Apply for Dexcom Recruitment 2026

Interested candidates can apply online through the official Dexcom Careers portal.

Official Apply Link:

CLICK HERE

Before submitting your application, ensure that your resume is updated with:

  • Technical skills
  • Software development projects
  • Internships
  • Professional work experience
  • GitHub profile (if available)
  • Certifications
  • Achievements

An ATS-friendly resume significantly improves the chances of being shortlisted during the initial screening process.

Why This Opportunity Stands Out

Unlike many traditional software engineering roles, this position allows engineers to build products that directly contribute to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide. Developers work with modern technologies including cloud computing, scalable backend systems, frontend frameworks, DevOps tools, and secure healthcare platforms.

Working at Dexcom also provides an opportunity to collaborate with experienced engineers from multiple countries while continuously enhancing technical and leadership skills.

For professionals looking to build a long-term career in software engineering with meaningful impact, Dexcom offers an excellent platform for growth.

Dexcom Corporation is hiring Software Development Engineer 2 for its Bengaluru office.

Q2. What is the required experience?

Candidates should have between 2 and 5 years of professional software development experience.

The job location is Bengaluru, Karnataka, India.

Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Node.js, Go, Scala, Ruby, and similar programming languages.

Cloud knowledge is preferred. Experience with AWS, Google Cloud Platform, Docker, Kubernetes, and CI/CD pipelines will be beneficial.

Q6. Is this a full-time role?

Yes. This is a full-time Software Development Engineer position.

Q7. How can I apply?

Candidates can submit their application through the official Dexcom Careers website using the application link provided above.

The Dexcom Recruitment 2026 drive presents an outstanding opportunity for experienced software engineers who aspire to work with one of the world’s leading healthcare technology companies. From developing cloud-native applications to contributing to products that improve millions of lives, this role offers technical challenges, career growth, and meaningful impact.

title.rendered: AKTU Startup Samvad 3.0 Registration Begins: Startups Can Pitch Before Investors, Event on September 8

content.rendered:
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow, has announced the third edition of UP Startup Samvad 3.0 – Connect Innovations with Investments, inviting startups, incubators and affiliated institutions to participate in one of Uttar Pradesh’s biggest startup networking events. The programme will be held on 8 September 2026 at the AKTU Campus in Lucknow, while registrations for startups will remain open until 16 August 2026, according to the official university notification.

The initiative has been launched by the Innovation Hub, AKTU, with the objective of bringing startups, investors, industry leaders, policymakers and innovation ecosystem partners onto a common platform. Through this event, entrepreneurs will get an opportunity to showcase innovative business ideas, interact with potential investors and explore funding opportunities that can help scale their ventures.

For early-stage startups, one of the biggest challenges is reaching the right investors. Startup Samvad 3.0 aims to address this gap by creating direct interaction between founders and funding agencies. Selected startups will be invited to present their ventures before Angel Investors, Venture Capitalists (VCs) and Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) during the pitching session, while also exhibiting their products and services at the Startup Expo.

According to the circular, the university has requested all constituent and affiliated institutions to circulate the information among startups associated with their network and encourage eligible entrepreneurs to complete their registration before the deadline. Only shortlisted startups will receive the opportunity to participate in the pitching session and Startup Expo.

AKTU Startup Samvad 3.0 Important Dates

Apart from investment opportunities, Startup Samvad 3.0 has been designed to provide startups with long-term growth opportunities. Participants will be able to connect with corporates, government departments, industry experts and startup ecosystem leaders, opening doors for collaboration and strategic partnerships. Entrepreneurs will also receive guidance on fundraising, market expansion, business strategy and government support schemes that can help strengthen their businesses.

Another major attraction of the event is the possibility of exploring grant support of up to ₹25 lakh under the Uttar Pradesh Startup Policy, as mentioned in the official notification. Startups will also get access to incubation support opportunities available across Uttar Pradesh, making the programme valuable not only for securing investment but also for long-term business development.

The event is equally significant for incubation centres and startup support organisations. Incubators participating in Startup Samvad 3.0 will have an opportunity to showcase their incubation ecosystem, promote student-led innovations, collaborate with investors and policymakers, mentor emerging startups and strengthen partnerships within Uttar Pradesh’s innovation ecosystem.

AKTU expects the event to witness participation from startup founders, investors, industry experts, government officials and innovation leaders from across the state. By bringing all stakeholders together on a single platform, the university aims to accelerate innovation, encourage entrepreneurship and create new investment opportunities for promising startups.

Startups interested in participating must complete their registration through the official Startup Samvad portal before 16 August 2026. As the number of pitching slots is limited, founders are advised to apply well before the closing date to improve their chances of selection.

With Startup Samvad 3.0, AKTU continues its efforts to strengthen the startup ecosystem in Uttar Pradesh by connecting innovative entrepreneurs with investors, mentors and policymakers. For startups seeking funding, strategic guidance and industry exposure, the event offers a valuable opportunity to take the next step in their entrepreneurial journey.

It is AKTU’s flagship startup networking and investment event that connects startups with investors, incubators, government stakeholders and industry leaders.

Q2. When will Startup Samvad 3.0 be held?
The event is scheduled for 8 September 2026 at the AKTU Campus, Lucknow.

Eligible startups can register until 16 August 2026.

The event is open to startups and incubation centres associated with AKTU and its affiliated institutions, as described in the official notification.

Q5. What are the key benefits for startups?
Selected startups can pitch before investors, participate in the Startup Expo, build industry connections, receive mentorship, explore incubation support and learn about government funding opportunities.

title.rendered: AKTU Challenge Evaluation Stage-2 2026 Notification Released: Students Can Apply Online Till August 18, Check Fee, Eligibility & Refund Rules

content.rendered:
The Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow has officially released an important notification regarding Challenge Evaluation (Stage-2) for the Even Semester Examination 2025-26. Students who believe that their answer sheets were not evaluated correctly can now apply for the second stage of challenge evaluation through the university’s online portal.

According to the official notification, the online application window has opened on August 4, 2026, and eligible students can submit their applications until August 18, 2026 by paying the prescribed fee.

If you are an AKTU student waiting for re-evaluation or expecting an improvement in your marks, here is everything you need to know about the latest notification.

AKTU Releases Challenge Evaluation Stage-2 Notice

AKTU has issued an official circular for students who appeared in the Even Semester Examination 2025-26. The notification informs affiliated colleges that eligible students can participate in the Challenge Evaluation Stage-2 process for their answer books.

The university has instructed all affiliated institutions to inform students about the application process and ensure they complete the online registration before the deadline.

What is AKTU Challenge Evaluation Stage-2?

Challenge Evaluation Stage-2 is a special evaluation process offered by AKTU to students who are dissatisfied with the marks awarded in their semester examinations.

Under this process, students can request a fresh evaluation of their answer books after completing the prescribed online application process and paying the required fee. The university conducts the evaluation as per its approved examination guidelines.

AKTU Challenge Evaluation Stage-2 2026: Important Dates

Students are advised not to wait until the last day to submit their applications, as heavy traffic on the portal may cause delays.

Application Fee

Students applying for Challenge Evaluation Stage-2 will have to pay:

₹2,500 per subject

The application fee must be paid online while submitting the application form. Applications without successful payment will not be considered.

Who Can Apply?

The notification is applicable to students who appeared in the Even Semester Examination 2025-26 and are eligible under the university’s Challenge Evaluation guidelines.

Students should carefully verify their subject details before submitting the application because the evaluation request will be processed based on the information provided during online registration.

How to Apply for AKTU Challenge Evaluation Stage-2

Students can complete the application by following these steps:

  1. Visit the AKTU Challenge Evaluation online portal.
  2. Log in using your examination credentials.
  3. Select the subject(s) for Challenge Evaluation.
  4. Verify all academic details carefully.
  5. Pay the application fee of ₹2,500 per subject.
  6. Submit the application and save the payment receipt for future reference.

The university has directed students to complete the process within the specified timeline.

Refund Policy Explained

One of the most important highlights of the notification is the refund provision.

According to AKTU, if the difference between the original marks and the revised marks after Challenge Evaluation is 20% or more, the student will receive a refund after deducting an administrative charge.

In such cases:

  • ₹2,500 is initially paid by the student.
  • ₹1,000 will be deducted as processing/administrative charges.
  • The remaining amount will be refunded.

Students must provide their Account Number, IFSC Code, and Bank Name correctly to receive the refund. Incorrect bank details may delay or prevent the refund process.

Final Marks After Challenge Evaluation

The notification clearly states that the marks awarded after completion of the Challenge Evaluation process will be treated as the final marks and will be applicable even if they are lower or higher than the previously awarded marks. Students should keep this important condition in mind before applying.

Documents and Information Required

Before starting the application process, students should keep the following details ready:

  • Enrollment Number
  • Roll Number
  • Subject Code
  • Registered Mobile Number
  • Payment Details
  • Account Number
  • IFSC Code
  • Bank Name

Having these details ready will help complete the application smoothly.

Important Instructions for Students

AKTU has advised students to:

  • Read all instructions carefully before applying.
  • Enter bank account details correctly.
  • Keep a copy of the payment receipt.
  • Complete the application before the deadline.
  • Contact their respective colleges if they face any difficulty during the application process.

Why This Notification Matters

Challenge Evaluation Stage-2 offers students an opportunity to ensure that their answer books have been evaluated accurately. For students whose academic progression, placement eligibility, scholarships, or higher education plans depend on their semester results, this process can be significant.

Since the revised marks become final after evaluation, applicants should carefully assess their situation before submitting the request.

Conclusion

AKTU has officially opened the Challenge Evaluation Stage-2 application process for the Even Semester Examination 2025-26, allowing eligible students to request a fresh evaluation of their answer books. With the application window open from August 4 to August 18, 2026, interested candidates should complete the online process within the stipulated timeline.

Students are also advised to carefully read the official guidelines, verify their details before submission, and keep all payment and application records safely for future reference.

title.rendered: AKTU Shivratri Notice 2026: Online Classes for Academic Session 2026–27 Due to Kanwar Yatra | Official Notification

content.rendered:
Students of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow should take note of an important notification issued by the university regarding the conduct of online classes for the Academic Session 2026–27. The advisory has been released in view of Shravan Shivratri, which will be celebrated on 11 August 2026, and the heavy movement of devotees during the Kanwar Yatra across Uttar Pradesh.

Considering the possibility of temporary closure of colleges, universities, and technical institutions by district administrations due to security and traffic management, AKTU has directed all affiliated institutions to continue academic activities through online classes wherever required. The university has emphasized that the academic calendar should remain unaffected and students’ studies should continue without interruption.

AKTU Releases Official Notification

The official circular has been issued by Prof. Deepak Nagariya, Controller of Examinations, Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Uttar Pradesh.

According to the notification, Shravan Shivratri will be observed on 11 August 2026. Since a large number of Kanwar pilgrims are expected to travel through different districts of Uttar Pradesh, local administrations may issue orders for the temporary closure of educational institutions to maintain law and order and ensure the safety of students, teachers, and the general public.

Keeping these circumstances in mind, AKTU has instructed all affiliated colleges and technical institutions to continue academic activities through online classes wherever offline classes cannot be conducted.

Why Has AKTU Issued This Advisory?

The university has clarified that the purpose of this notification is not merely to inform institutions about Shivratri. Instead, the advisory focuses on maintaining uninterrupted teaching during the Academic Session 2026–27.

Every year, the Kanwar Yatra leads to increased traffic, road diversions, and security arrangements in several districts. As a result, district administrations may temporarily suspend offline classes in educational institutions.

To prevent any disruption in teaching and learning, AKTU has instructed institutions to adopt online teaching wherever necessary. This decision ensures that students continue their education without affecting the academic schedule.

Shravan Shivratri and Kanwar Yatra: Reason Behind the Advisory

The university has mentioned that Shravan Shivratri falls on 11 August 2026, a day when lakhs of devotees participate in the Kanwar Yatra across Uttar Pradesh.

Because of the large movement of Kanwariyas, district administrations may issue orders to close educational institutions in affected areas.

However, instead of suspending academic activities, AKTU has instructed institutions to continue teaching through online mode wherever required. This ensures both student safety and uninterrupted academic progress.

Online Classes for Academic Session 2026–27

The central objective of the notification is to ensure that all teaching activities continue according to the Academic Calendar 2026–27.

AKTU has directed affiliated colleges to make necessary arrangements for online teaching whenever offline classes cannot be conducted due to local administrative restrictions.

The university has also stressed that students should not suffer any academic loss because of temporary institutional closures.

This decision reflects AKTU’s commitment to digital learning and uninterrupted academic delivery throughout the semester.

Key Instructions Issued by AKTU

The official notification contains several important directions that every affiliated institution must follow.

Continue Academic Activities

All teaching and learning activities should continue according to the Academic Calendar 2026–27 without unnecessary interruption.

Conduct Online Classes Wherever Required

Institutions should organize online classes whenever physical classes cannot be conducted because of administrative orders issued by the District Magistrate or local authorities.

Inform Students Through Official Channels

Students should be informed about online class schedules through:

  • Official College Website
  • ERP Portal
  • Official Email
  • WhatsApp Groups
  • Other Authorized Communication Platforms

Protect Students’ Academic Interests

Institutions must ensure that students’ academic activities are not affected and that the semester continues smoothly.

Complete Academic and Examination Activities on Time

Colleges have been instructed to complete teaching, internal assessments, practical sessions, and examination-related work according to the prescribed university schedule.

Will AKTU Colleges Remain Closed on 11 August 2026?

The official notification does not announce a university-wide holiday.

Instead, AKTU has clarified that the closure of colleges depends on orders issued by the respective District Magistrate (DM) or local administration.

If educational institutions are directed to remain closed because of the Kanwar Yatra, colleges should continue teaching through online classes so that students do not lose valuable academic time.

Responsibilities of Affiliated Colleges

The university has requested all Directors and Principals to ensure strict compliance with the advisory.

Institutions should:

  • Follow local administrative orders.
  • Arrange online classes wherever necessary.
  • Inform students through official communication channels.
  • Continue teaching according to the Academic Calendar 2026–27.
  • Ensure that academic and examination activities remain on schedule.

The university has also instructed institutions to issue their own notices wherever required to ensure smooth implementation of these directions.

What Should Students Do?

Students are advised to remain connected with their respective institutions and regularly check official sources for updates.

They should:

  • Visit the college website frequently.
  • Monitor the ERP Portal.
  • Check official email notifications.
  • Stay active in official WhatsApp groups.
  • Attend online classes as per the institution’s schedule.

Students should avoid relying on unofficial social media posts and instead follow only official announcements issued by AKTU and their colleges.

Benefits of the University’s Decision

The advisory offers several important benefits for students and institutions.

  • Ensures uninterrupted teaching during administrative restrictions.
  • Prevents loss of valuable academic days.
  • Supports timely completion of the syllabus.
  • Keeps the Academic Calendar 2026–27 on schedule.
  • Ensures smooth conduct of examinations and internal assessments.
  • Protects students’ academic interests during the festival period.

By allowing institutions to switch to online classes whenever necessary, AKTU has balanced public safety with uninterrupted education.

Conclusion

The AKTU Shivratri Notice 2026 is an important academic advisory that focuses on two key objectives—ensuring student safety during Shravan Shivratri and the Kanwar Yatra, and maintaining uninterrupted teaching through online classes for the Academic Session 2026–27.

Rather than declaring a university-wide holiday, AKTU has instructed affiliated colleges to continue teaching through online mode wherever offline classes cannot be conducted because of local administrative restrictions. Institutions have also been directed to inform students through official communication channels and ensure that academic and examination activities continue according to the Academic Calendar 2026–27.

Students should regularly check their college website, ERP Portal, official email, and WhatsApp groups for the latest updates regarding online classes and institutional notices.

Why has AKTU issued this notification?

AKTU has issued the advisory to ensure uninterrupted academic activities during Shravan Shivratri and the Kanwar Yatra while protecting students’ academic interests.

Has AKTU declared a holiday on 11 August 2026?

No. The university has not declared a common holiday. The closure of colleges depends on orders issued by the respective district administration.

Will online classes be conducted?

Yes. Institutions have been directed to conduct online classes wherever offline classes cannot be organized because of local administrative restrictions.

How will students receive information?

Students will receive updates through the college website, ERP Portal, official email, WhatsApp groups, and other authorized communication channels.

Will the Academic Calendar 2026–27 change?

No. AKTU has instructed institutions to continue teaching according to the Academic Calendar 2026–27 and complete academic as well as examination-related activities on schedule.
