title.rendered: Penalty for Wrong Evaluation of Answer Sheets: Governor’s Statement Brings Hope for Students

content.rendered:
Penalty for Wrong Evaluation of Answer Sheets – The issue of wrong evaluation of answer sheets has been a long-standing problem in the Indian education system. Every year, thousands of students complain that their answer sheets were not evaluated properly, leading to unfair results, backlogs, and loss of academic opportunities. Recently, the Governor of Uttar Pradesh made an important statement suggesting that penalties should be imposed for incorrect evaluation of exam copies.

This statement has sparked serious discussion across universities, especially among students of state universities. The proposal is being seen as a major reform that could make the examination system more transparent, fair, and student-centric.

What Is Wrong Evaluation of Answer Sheets?

Wrong evaluation of answer sheets does not mean only giving fewer marks. It includes several types of mistakes made during the checking process.

Common Types of Wrong Evaluation

These mistakes directly affect a student’s result and future.

Why Wrong Evaluation Is a Serious Issue

The examination result plays a crucial role in a student’s academic and professional life. A single incorrect evaluation can change the direction of a student’s career.

Impact of Wrong Evaluation on Students

For students from economically weaker backgrounds, these consequences are even more severe.

Governor’s Statement on Penalty for Wrong Evaluation

The Governor clearly stated that there should be a provision for penalty in cases of wrong evaluation of answer sheets. According to him, simply correcting mistakes is not enough. Accountability must be fixed so that such errors do not happen repeatedly.

This statement is important because, until now:

  • Students suffered the loss
  • Evaluators rarely faced consequences
  • The system lacked strict accountability

The idea of penalty aims to balance responsibility between students and the examination authorities.

How Penalty for Wrong Evaluation Can Improve the System

Introducing a penalty for wrong evaluation of answer sheets can bring multiple improvements to the education system.

Expected Benefits

This reform can significantly reduce careless checking practices.

Role of Digital Evaluation in Preventing Wrong Evaluation

Digital evaluation is being promoted as an effective solution to reduce wrong evaluation of answer sheets. Many universities have already started adopting digital systems.

Advantages of Digital Evaluation

Digital evaluation, combined with penalties for wrong evaluation, can greatly strengthen the examination process.

Impact on State Universities and Large Exam Systems

State universities conduct examinations for lakhs of students every year. Due to high volume, evaluation errors are more common.

If the policy of penalty for wrong evaluation of answer sheets is implemented:

  • Evaluation quality will improve
  • Student grievances will reduce
  • Examination credibility will increase

This reform can set a benchmark for other states and institutions to follow.

Is This Policy Against Teachers?

No, this policy is not against honest teachers. Most evaluators perform their duties sincerely and responsibly. The proposed penalty system mainly targets:

  • Repeated negligence
  • Careless checking
  • Intentional or irresponsible evaluation

Positive Impact on Honest Evaluators

The goal is to improve the system, not to punish genuine educators.

Implementation Status of the Penalty Rule

At present, the statement reflects a policy direction, not an immediate rule. The implementation process may involve:

  • Drafting evaluation guidelines
  • Consulting universities and education experts
  • Defining types of errors and penalties
  • Expanding digital evaluation infrastructure

Although it may take time, the intent to reform is clearly visible.

What Students Should Do Going Forward

Students should stay informed and prepared.

Student Action Checklist

The most positive outcome is that students’ voices are now being heard at the highest level.

Why This Reform Is Important for Parents

Parents invest heavily in their children’s education. Wrong evaluation not only affects students but also places emotional and financial stress on families.

This reform ensures:

  • Fair academic assessment
  • Reduced uncertainty in results
  • Greater confidence in public education institutions

It is a reassuring step for parents who worry about unjust academic outcomes.

Long-Term Impact of Penalty for Wrong Evaluation of Answer Sheets

If implemented effectively, this reform can lead to:

  • Stronger education governance
  • Better academic outcomes
  • Reduced legal disputes
  • Improved national and global reputation of universities

A fair evaluation system is the foundation of quality education.

FAQ

Q1. What is meant by wrong evaluation of answer sheets?
Wrong evaluation refers to mistakes like unchecked answers, incorrect marking, totalling errors, or careless checking of exam copies.

Q2. Has the penalty for wrong evaluation been implemented?
Currently, it is a policy-level proposal. Implementation will follow official guidelines and university approval.

Q3. How will penalties help students?
Penalties will improve evaluator accountability, reduce errors, and ensure fair results for students.

Q4. Will digital evaluation reduce wrong evaluation?
Yes, digital evaluation minimizes human error, improves transparency, and prevents totalling mistakes.

Conclusion

The proposal to introduce a penalty for wrong evaluation of answer sheets is a landmark step towards reforming the Indian examination system. It directly addresses one of the most painful issues faced by students for years.

By ensuring accountability, promoting digital evaluation, and protecting student interests, this move can create a fair, transparent, and trustworthy academic environment. If implemented properly, it will ensure that no student’s future is damaged due to careless or incorrect evaluation.

title.rendered: AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology 2026 – Full Syllabus, Credits & Eligibility

content.rendered:
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Uttar Pradesh has taken a major academic step by proposing the AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology for undergraduate engineering students. This initiative is in line with AICTE guidelines, the National Credit Framework (NCrF), and the vision of National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, with implementation proposed from the Academic Session 2026–27 .

The AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology is designed to equip students with multidisciplinary, future-ready skills in one of the fastest-growing and most strategic technology domains—space science and technology. This blog provides a complete, SEO-optimized, Google Discover–friendly guide covering official notification details, eligibility, credit structure, full syllabus overview, and career opportunities.

Official AKTU Notification: What Has Been Announced?

As per the official circular issued by the Dean, UGS&E, AKTU (Ref. No. AKTU/DEAN UG/2024/821 dated 07 January 2026), the University has invited views and suggestions from affiliated institutions regarding the proposed UG Minor Degree Programme in Space Technology .

Key Highlights of the Circular

  • Programme Name: AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology
  • Level: Undergraduate (UG)
  • Implementation Year: 2026–27
  • Total Credits: 18
  • Total Courses: 5
  • Eligible Branches: All Engineering Branches
  • Feedback Deadline: 15 January 2026
  • Official Email: dean.ugse@aktu.ac.in

This step indicates AKTU’s commitment to introducing industry-relevant, multidisciplinary programs under NEP 2020.

Programme Overview: AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology

Space technology has emerged as a critical enabler of national development, strategic capability, and global competitiveness. Applications of space systems are no longer limited to rocket launches; they directly impact communication, navigation, earth observation, disaster management, climate monitoring, agriculture, defense, and planetary exploration .

The AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology aims to:

  • Strengthen India’s indigenous space ecosystem
  • Create a skilled, industry-ready workforce
  • Promote multidisciplinary and application-oriented learning
  • Integrate engineering fundamentals with real-world space missions

Under this program, students gain exposure to launch vehicles, spacecraft systems, orbital mechanics, remote sensing, GIS, GNSS, AI/ML-based space data analytics, and space law.

Concept of Minor Degree as per AICTE & NEP 2020

AICTE introduced the Minor Degree concept to enhance employability and allow students to gain deep expertise in emerging areas not covered in traditional UG curricula.

Important Rules:

  • Minor Degree requires 18–20 additional credits
  • These credits are in addition to 160 UG credits
  • AICTE approval is not mandatory
  • Can be pursued alongside the main degree

The AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology strictly follows this framework and meets all academic norms defined under NCrF and NEP 2020 .

Eligibility Criteria for AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology

Students interested in the AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology must fulfill the following conditions:

  • Must be enrolled in any UG Engineering program
  • Eligible from 4th Semester onwards
  • Must have completed:
    • Engineering Mathematics
    • Engineering Physics
    • Introductory Programming (as per university norms)

After successful completion of all required credits, students will be awarded a Minor Degree in Space Technology along with their main undergraduate degree.

Study & Evaluation Scheme (18 Credits)

Detailed Syllabus: AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology

SPT001 – Introduction to Space Technology (3 Credits)

This foundational course introduces students to the core concepts of space technology.

Major Topics Include:

  • Basics of launch vehicle design and missiles
  • Mission trajectory design and orbital mechanics
  • Remote sensing systems and space data products
  • Digital image processing, photogrammetry, and GNSS
  • Space law, Indian Space Policy 2022, space tourism

Learning Outcome: Students understand space missions, systems, and regulatory frameworks.

SPT002 – Launch Vehicle Systems and Technologies (3 Credits)

This course focuses on the engineering and dynamics of launch vehicles.

Key Areas:

  • Solid, liquid, cryogenic, semi-cryogenic & electric propulsion
  • Launch vehicle dynamics and aerodynamics
  • Guidance, Navigation & Control (GNC) systems
  • Simulation testbeds (HILS, SILS, OILS)
  • Descent and landing of jettisoned stages

Learning Outcome: Students gain hands-on conceptual knowledge of launch systems.

SPT003 – Spaceflight Mechanics & Attitude Dynamics (4 Credits)

This advanced course explains spacecraft motion and control.

Key Areas:

  • Orbital mechanics and perturbations
  • Attitude dynamics and stabilization techniques
  • Reaction wheels, thrusters, and sensors
  • Missile guidance and re-entry flight mechanics
  • Chandrayaan and Mars mission case studies

Learning Outcome: Ability to analyze spacecraft trajectories and control systems.

SPT004 – Spacecraft Systems Engineering (4 Credits)

This course provides a complete spacecraft lifecycle perspective.

Key Areas:

  • Satellite subsystems and onboard computers
  • Structures, materials, and thermal control
  • Satellite communication principles
  • Remote sensing and quantum communication
  • Ground segment, integration, and quality assurance

Learning Outcome: Students understand end-to-end spacecraft system design.

SPT005 – Space Data Products and Services (4 Credits)

This course bridges space technology with data science and AI.

Key Areas:

  • Remote sensing and image interpretation
  • Digital image processing and classification
  • Photogrammetry, GIS, GNSS (NavIC, GAGAN)
  • AI/ML, deep learning, cloud platforms
  • Applications in agriculture, climate, oceans & planetary science

Learning Outcome: Practical skills in space data analytics and geospatial applications.

Career Scope After AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology

Completing the AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology opens doors to multiple career paths:

  • Satellite Data Analyst
  • Remote Sensing & GIS Engineer
  • GNSS & Navigation Analyst
  • Space Systems Engineer (Entry-Level)
  • Research Assistant in Space Science

It also strengthens applications for ISRO, DRDO, private space startups, and higher studies (M.Tech/MS in Aerospace, Space Technology, or Geospatial Engineering).

Why AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology is a Game-Changer

  • Multidisciplinary learning without changing core branch
  • High-demand skills aligned with future technologies
  • Strong industry and research relevance
  • Fully compliant with NEP 2020 and AICTE norms
  • Enhances employability and academic profile

The AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology positions students at the forefront of India’s growing space ecosystem.

READ MORE : AKTU Scholarship Verification 2025–26: Important Notice for Affiliated Colleges and Students

Final Conclusion

The proposed AKTU Minor Degree in Space Technology is a visionary academic initiative that reflects AKTU’s commitment to future-ready education. With a comprehensive 18-credit curriculum, deep technical coverage, and real-world applications, this program can significantly enhance the career prospects of undergraduate engineering students from Academic Session 2026–27 onwards.

Students and institutions should regularly follow official AKTU updates regarding final approval and enrollment procedures.

title.rendered: AKTU National Youth Day 2026: Run for Swadeshi | Full Guidelines & Student Participation

content.rendered:
AKTU National Youth Day 2026 – Every year, 12 January is celebrated across India as National Youth Day in memory of Swami Vivekananda, whose ideas continue to inspire millions of young minds. In line with this spirit, Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), in coordination with All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), has issued an official circular regarding the organization of a nationwide youth outreach programme titled “Run for Swadeshi (Swadeshi Sankalp Run)” on National Youth Day 2026.

This initiative is not just a symbolic run, but a powerful movement aimed at strengthening Indian values, Swadeshi mindset, and Atmanirbhar Bharat vision among students and youth.

In this article, we will explain everything in detail – meaning of the programme, objectives, eligibility, activities, institutional responsibilities, and why AKTU students must actively participate.

What is AKTU National Youth Day 2026 & Why 12 January Matters?

National Youth Day is observed every year on 12 January, the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda, one of India’s greatest spiritual leaders and youth icons. His teachings on self-discipline, nationalism, character-building, and self-reliance are more relevant than ever in today’s fast-changing global environment.

Swami Vivekananda believed that:

“Give me 100 energetic young men and I shall transform India.”

Keeping this philosophy in mind, AKTU and AICTE aim to mobilize youth power through collective participation in meaningful national activities.

What is “Run for Swadeshi (Swadeshi Sankalp Run)”?

Run for Swadeshi, also called Swadeshi Sankalp Run, is a nationwide youth awareness programme proposed to be organized on 12 January 2026.

The programme encourages students and youth to:

  • Support Indian-made products
  • Understand the importance of Swadeshi
  • Contribute towards Atmanirbhar Bharat
  • Develop a sense of national responsibility

This is not merely a race or walk, but a symbolic commitment (Sankalp) taken by youth for the nation’s progress.

Key Objectives of Run for Swadeshi Programme

The primary objectives of this initiative include:

  1. Promoting Indian Values
    To spread awareness about India’s cultural heritage, ethics, and values among students.
  2. Encouraging Swadeshi Spirit
    To motivate youth to prefer and promote Indian products and services.
  3. Strengthening Atmanirbhar Bharat
    To align students with the national vision of self-reliance in manufacturing, innovation, and entrepreneurship.
  4. Youth Empowerment
    To inspire leadership qualities, discipline, teamwork, and civic responsibility.
  5. National Unity & Social Cohesion
    To bring students, faculty, and citizens together for a common national cause.

Who Can Participate in Run for Swadeshi 2026?

As per the official instructions, participation is open and inclusive. The following groups can actively take part:

  • University & College Students
  • NSS and NCC Cadets
  • Youth Club Members
  • Faculty and Staff Members
  • General Public

AKTU-affiliated institutions are encouraged to ensure maximum student participation.

Activities Planned Under Swadeshi Sankalp Run

Institutions have the flexibility to organize activities based on their local feasibility. Suggested activities include:

🏃‍♂️ Run / Walk Events

  • Distance options: 2 km, 3 km, or 5 km
  • Can be conducted inside campus or public areas

🎤 Awareness & Motivational Sessions

  • Talks on Swadeshi, Atmanirbhar Bharat, and youth responsibility
  • Discussion on Swami Vivekananda’s teachings

📢 Dissemination of Messages

  • Posters, banners, slogans promoting Indian products
  • Student-led awareness campaigns

📝 Registration & Certificates

  • Participant registration
  • Distribution of participation certificates (as applicable)

Role of AKTU-Affiliated Colleges & Universities

AKTU has requested all Vice-Chancellors, Directors, and Principals to actively support and organize this programme.

Institutional Responsibilities:

  • Organize Run for Swadeshi on or around 12 January 2026
  • Ensure student safety and discipline
  • Coordinate with NSS/NCC units
  • Encourage wide participation
  • Maintain proper documentation of the event

Post-Event Reporting & Submission

After successful completion of the programme, institutions are required to:

  • Upload event photographs
  • Submit brief activity details
  • Fill the official Google Form
  • Upload information on official website & social media handles

This reporting helps AKTU and AICTE track participation and national outreach impact.

Why This Programme Is Important for Students

For students, participation in such national initiatives offers multiple benefits:

  • Builds leadership and teamwork skills
  • Enhances social responsibility
  • Strengthens understanding of India’s economic self-reliance
  • Adds value to academic and co-curricular profile
  • Encourages patriotism beyond textbooks

In today’s competitive world, employers and institutions value students who actively engage in nation-building activities.

Message from AICTE & AKTU

The programme has been issued with the approval and encouragement of AICTE officials and AKTU authorities, emphasizing that youth participation is crucial for shaping India’s future.

The initiative aligns with:

  • Nation-building
  • Youth empowerment
  • Sustainable development
  • Cultural awareness

Final Words: A Call to India’s Youth

The Run for Swadeshi (Swadeshi Sankalp Run) 2026 is more than an event—it is a movement. It reflects India’s belief that youth are the backbone of national progress.

AKTU students are strongly encouraged to participate actively, take the Swadeshi Sankalp, and become ambassadors of Atmanirbhar Bharat.

As Swami Vivekananda envisioned, the future of India lies in the strength, discipline, and values of its youth—and this initiative is a step in that direction.

content.rendered:

Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow has issued an important and mandatory notice related to the Post-Matric Scholarship and Fee Reimbursement Scheme for the academic session 2025–26. This notice is especially important for all government and self-financed colleges affiliated with AKTU, as it directly affects the scholarship applications of thousands of students.

The university has clearly instructed institutions to verify the actual number of students, confirm their eligibility, and submit a legally valid affidavit within the given deadline. Any mistake or delay may result in rejection of scholarship applications and institutional liability.

Issuing Authority Details

The notification has been released by Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Uttar Pradesh.

University Address:
Sector-11, Jankipuram Extension Scheme,
Lucknow – 226031

Reference Number: AKTU / Kus.Ka./Scholarship / 2026 / 9843
Date of Issue: January 2026
Nature of Notice: Necessary and Important

What Is the AKTU Scholarship Verification Notice 2025–26?

The AKTU Scholarship Verification Notice 2025–26 is an official instruction issued to ensure that only genuine and eligible students receive benefits under the Post-Matric Scholarship and Fee Reimbursement Scheme.

As per directions from the Social Welfare Department (Samaj Kalyan Anubhag-3), the university and its affiliated institutions must:

  • Verify the actual enrollment of students
  • Check the eligibility of each scholarship applicant
  • Identify and block ineligible students, courses, or institutions
  • Complete the entire process through online verification

This step has been introduced to prevent duplicate applications, false claims, and misuse of government funds.

Why AKTU Scholarship Verification 2025–26 Is So Important

Scholarship schemes involve public funds, and therefore accuracy and transparency are extremely important. If an institution forwards incorrect or false data, it can lead to serious consequences.

The verification process helps to ensure that:

  • Only deserving students receive financial assistance
  • Government funds are used correctly
  • Institutions remain accountable for the data they submit

Any negligence may result in financial recovery, penalties, or strict administrative action against the institution.

Revised Scholarship Verification Timeline

The Social Welfare Department has revised the verification schedule. All institutions must strictly follow the updated dates mentioned below:

Institutions are advised not to wait until the last date, as failure to meet the deadline will make the institution fully responsible.

Which Institutions Must Follow This Notice?

This notice is applicable to:

  • All colleges affiliated with AKTU
  • Government institutions
  • Self-financed and private institutions
  • Institutions forwarding Post-Matric Scholarship applications

No affiliated institution is exempt from this process.

Mandatory Affidavit Requirement Explained Simply

One of the most important parts of this notice is the submission of an affidavit by the Director or Principal of the institution.

Through this affidavit, the institution must officially declare that:

  1. All students listed in the forwarded scholarship applications are genuinely studying in the institution.
  2. The online scholarship applications submitted by students have been carefully checked and matched with official records.
  3. Only eligible students, as per the scholarship guidelines, have been forwarded.
  4. None of the forwarded students has applied for any other Central Government scholarship scheme.
  5. No ineligible student has been forwarded under the scholarship scheme.

The affidavit must also clearly mention that:

  • All information provided is true and complete
  • No facts have been hidden
  • If any ineligible student is found in the future, the institution will be fully responsible

This makes the affidavit a legally binding document.

Documents to Be Submitted to AKTU

Each institution must submit the following documents to the university:

  • Original signed affidavit by the Director or Principal
  • Complete list of students benefiting from the scholarship
  • The list must be prepared class-wise and year-wise
  • The list must be verified and signed by the Director/Principal

Last Date for Submission:
05 February 2026 (mandatory in all cases)

What Happens If an Institution Does Not Comply?

If an institution fails to complete verification or submit the required documents:

  • Scholarship applications may be rejected
  • The institution may be held financially liable
  • Administrative or legal action may be taken
  • The institution’s future participation in scholarship schemes may be affected

Therefore, institutions are strongly advised to complete the process carefully and on time.

Important Information for Students

Although the notice is addressed to institutions, students should also remain alert. Students should:

  • Ensure all details in their scholarship application are correct
  • Avoid applying for multiple scholarship schemes
  • Stay in regular contact with the college scholarship department
  • Monitor updates on the AKTU and Social Welfare portals

Any incorrect information provided by a student may lead to rejection of the scholarship.

Key Points at a Glance

  • AKTU has issued a mandatory scholarship verification notice for 2025–26
  • Applies to all AKTU-affiliated government and private colleges
  • Online verification period: 28 January to 07 February 2026
  • Affidavit and verified list submission deadline: 05 February 2026
  • Institutions will be fully responsible for incorrect or false data

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the purpose of AKTU Scholarship Verification 2025–26?
To ensure that only genuine and eligible students receive Post-Matric Scholarship benefits.

Who must submit the affidavit?
The Director or Principal of each AKTU-affiliated institution.

Is this notice applicable to private colleges?
Yes, it applies to both government and self-financed institutions.

What if an ineligible student is found later?
The concerned institution will be fully responsible, including financial liability.

What is the final submission date?
05 February 2026.

Final Conclusion

The AKTU Scholarship Verification 2025–26 notice is a crucial step to ensure fairness, transparency, and accountability in the scholarship system. Institutions must take this responsibility seriously by verifying student data accurately and submitting all required documents within the deadline.

For students, staying informed and submitting correct information is equally important. Timely compliance by both colleges and students will ensure smooth processing of scholarships without delays or complications.

title.rendered: DAERA Postgraduate Studentships 2026: Research Opportunities Shaping a Sustainable Future

content.rendered:
The DAERA Postgraduate Studentships 2026 offer an exceptional opportunity for postgraduate students and early-career researchers to engage in high-impact, policy-driven research that directly contributes to sustainability, climate action, and rural development in Northern Ireland. Announced by the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (DAERA), these studentships are designed to build future research leaders while addressing some of the most pressing environmental, agricultural, and societal challenges of our time.

If you are passionate about sustainable agri-food systems, climate change, One Health, environmental protection, or rural wellbeing, this fully funded postgraduate research opportunity for 2026 could be the ideal next step in your academic journey.

About DAERA Postgraduate Studentships 2026

The DAERA Postgraduate Studentship Programme 2026 is built around applied research with real-world impact. Unlike purely theoretical projects, these studentships emphasize research that informs government policy, industry practice, and community decision-making.

Successful candidates will work closely with policymakers, researchers, and stakeholders, ensuring their work contributes to tangible outcomes such as improved environmental management, resilient rural communities, and climate-smart agriculture.

Key Research Themes Under DAERA Studentships 2026

1. Sustainable Agri-Food Systems

Transforming agri-food systems is a cornerstone of DAERA’s 2026 research agenda. These studentships aim to balance increased productivity with reduced environmental impact.

Research opportunities include:

  • Enhancing soil carbon storage through plant breeding, soil microbiome research, and integrated farming systems
  • Developing novel soil and ecosystem health indicators, including biodiversity-focused metrics
  • Studying farmer behaviour change, adoption of sustainable practices, and incentive design using behavioural economics
  • Research on farmer mental health and wellbeing during climate and policy transitions
  • Innovations in livestock genetics, low-emission animal health technologies, and sustainable agri-infrastructure
  • Development of biofortified foods, agri-food product reformulation, and data-driven supply chains

This theme is ideal for candidates with backgrounds in agriculture, environmental science, economics, psychology, and food technology.

2. Climate Change and Green Growth

Aligned with Northern Ireland’s Green Growth Strategy and Net Zero commitments, DAERA Studentships 2026 support cutting-edge climate research across land, water, and marine systems.

Key focus areas:

  • Climate decision-support models and spatial mapping tools
  • Carbon markets, private finance, and green investment pathways
  • Forestry and agroforestry expansion strategies
  • Climate impacts on soil health, water quality, fisheries, and marine ecosystems
  • Adaptive strategies for climate resilience in agriculture and rural landscapes
  • Advanced greenhouse gas inventories and carbon accounting
  • Engineered carbon removal solutions such as biochar and direct air capture

Social science research is strongly encouraged, especially studies related to Just Transition, stakeholder acceptance, and fairness in land-use change.

3. One Health Research Opportunities

The One Health approach recognizes the interconnectedness of human, animal, and environmental health. DAERA’s 2026 studentships emphasize interdisciplinary research that bridges these domains.

Research priorities include:

  • Biosecurity behaviours among farmers
  • Climate-driven changes in disease vectors
  • Integrated disease surveillance using environmental and health data
  • Zoonotic disease emergence and antimicrobial resistance
  • Livestock welfare and pathogen genomics
  • Climate impacts on pollinators, including bees

These projects are particularly suitable for students from public health, veterinary science, epidemiology, environmental health, genomics, and social sciences.

4. Protecting and Restoring the Natural Environment

DAERA places strong emphasis on nature-based solutions and long-term ecosystem restoration.

Research areas include:

  • Water quality improvement and nutrient management at catchment scale
  • Innovative solutions for Lough Neagh
  • Peatland restoration and forest ecosystem services
  • Biodiversity conservation and habitat restoration
  • Marine protected area management
  • Circular bioeconomy solutions, including bio-refining agricultural and marine waste
  • Reducing ammonia emissions through advanced manure processing
  • Public attitudes towards air quality, biodiversity valuation, and land management

5. Strengthening Rural Affairs and Communities

Rural wellbeing and resilience are central to the DAERA Studentship Programme 2026.

Priority topics include:

  • Hidden poverty, inequality, and deprivation in rural areas
  • Social and health impacts of climate change on rural populations
  • Youth retention, skills development, and rural innovation
  • Cultural heritage and identity in rural Northern Ireland
  • Developing a future vision for rural policy aligned with sustainability goals

This theme welcomes applicants from sociology, economics, public policy, geography, and development studies.

Why Apply for DAERA Postgraduate Studentships 2026?

Choosing the DAERA Postgraduate Studentships 2026 offers multiple advantages:

Who Should Apply?

The DAERA Postgraduate Studentships 2026 are ideal for:

  • Graduates planning to pursue PhD or postgraduate research
  • Candidates interested in applied, impact-driven research
  • Students passionate about climate change, sustainability, health, and rural development
  • Researchers seeking strong links between academia and policy

If you are looking for a meaningful postgraduate research opportunity with global relevance, this is one programme you should not miss.

title.rendered: Siemens Internship 2026: Technical Intern for Bachelor Students, Bangalore

content.rendered:
In today’s competitive engineering and technology landscape, practical industry exposure matters as much as academic knowledge. That’s where the Siemens Internship 2026 comes in. Offered by Siemens, a global powerhouse with more than 170 years of innovation, this internship is designed for Bachelor students who want real-world experience in data engineering, automation, software, and digital industries.

The Siemens 2026 Internship – Technical Intern (Bangalore) is not just another internship. It is a structured, skill-focused program backed by Siemens’ official careers portal and trusted intern experiences. With Bangalore being Siemens’ key R&D and digital hub in India, this opportunity can genuinely shape your future career.

What is the Siemens Internship 2026?

The Siemens Internship 2026 is a 6-month Technical Intern program aimed at Bachelor (and select Master’s) students with an interest in data engineering, analytics, automation, and Industry 4.0 technologies.

This internship is hosted at Siemens Bangalore, one of India’s most important digital industries and R&D centers. Unlike generic internships that focus only on observation, this program allows interns to:

  • Work on live industry projects
  • Contribute to data engineering & analytics solutions
  • Explore AI, ML, cloud, and big data technologies
  • Collaborate with global Siemens teams

Interns often work on projects linked to smart infrastructure, mobility, energy optimization, and digital transformation, making the experience highly relevant and future-oriented.

Who Can Apply for Siemens Internship 2026?

The Siemens Internship 2026 is ideal for students who meet the following criteria:

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor’s Degree (B.E / B.Tech) in:
    • Computer Science & Engineering
    • Information Technology
    • Data Science
    • Electronics / Electrical / Related Engineering fields
  • Master’s degree students may also be considered for select roles

Experience Level

  • 0 – 2 years of hands-on experience

    • Data Engineering
    • Data Analytics
    • Databases
    • Cloud or Big Data technologies

This makes the Siemens Internship 2026 perfect for final-year students, freshers, and early-career candidates.

  • Ability to work independently
  • Comfortable collaborating with global teams
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills

These skills help interns adapt quickly to Siemens’ professional and multicultural work environment.

Role & Responsibilities in the Siemens Internship

As a Technical Intern / Data Engineer Intern, your responsibilities may include:

  • Using AI/ML methods and big data technologies
  • Implementing scalable cloud-based databases
  • Managing structured and unstructured datasets

Siemens also encourages interns to stay curious, innovative, and solution-oriented, which adds tremendous learning value.

title.rendered: AKTU Internal Marks Upload Date Extended Odd Sem 2025–26: Complete Official Update

content.rendered:
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow has released an important official notification announcing that the AKTU internal marks upload date extended Odd Sem 2025–26. This update is highly significant for all affiliated colleges and students, as internal (sessional) marks directly impact final results.

The decision to extend the deadline has been taken after several institutions requested additional time to complete the internal assessment process accurately. With this extension, AKTU aims to ensure error-free uploading of marks and smooth result processing.

In this detailed article, you will find complete information about the AKTU internal marks upload date extended Odd Sem 2025–26, including revised deadlines, instructions for colleges, impact on students, and official contact details.

AKTU Official Notice Overview

What Is the AKTU Internal Assessment System?

AKTU follows a continuous internal evaluation system along with end-semester examinations. Under this system:

  • Colleges conduct internal theory tests
  • Practical subjects include sessional practical exams
  • Faculty evaluates students internally
  • Marks are uploaded on the AKTU ERP portal
  • Final results include both internal and external marks

Because internal marks carry significant weightage, any delay or mistake can directly affect a student’s SGPA and result declaration. That is why the AKTU internal marks upload date extended Odd Sem 2025–26 is an important relief for colleges and students.

Why Was the AKTU Internal Marks Deadline Extended?

AKTU initially fixed a deadline for uploading and submitting internal marks. However, many institutions reported difficulties such as:

  • Delay in completing internal exams
  • ERP portal technical issues
  • Need for re-verification of marks
  • Incomplete practical assessments

After reviewing these concerns, the university officially announced that the AKTU internal marks upload date extended Odd Sem 2025–26 to avoid academic loss to students.

This extension reflects AKTU’s student-centric approach and commitment to academic fairness.

Revised Dates: AKTU Internal Marks Upload Date Extended for Odd Semester 2025–26

✅ New Official Deadlines

📌 These dates are applicable for:

  • Theory Sessional Marks
  • Practical Sessional Marks
  • All applicable Odd Semester courses

❗ First-semester students are excluded as per earlier AKTU guidelines.

Who Is Covered Under This AKTU Notice?

The AKTU internal marks upload date extended Odd Sem 2025–26 applies to:

  • Students studying in Odd Semester 2025–26
  • Undergraduate and postgraduate programs
  • All AKTU-affiliated colleges
  • Courses having internal theory or practical components

Students of the first semester are not included under this notice.

Step-by-Step Instructions for Colleges

AKTU has instructed all institutions to strictly follow the revised process:

Step 1: Online Upload

  • Login to the AKTU ERP portal
  • Enter internal marks carefully
  • Verify roll numbers, subject codes, and marks
  • Complete upload by 05 January 2026

Step 2: Hard Copy Preparation

  • Take printout of uploaded marks
  • Get documents signed by competent authorities
  • Arrange course-wise and semester-wise
  • Bind using spiral binding

Step 3: Final Submission

  • Submit two signed hard copies
  • Ensure delivery to AKTU office
  • Last date: 12 January 2026

Failure to comply even after the AKTU internal marks upload date extended for Odd Semester 2025–26 may lead to complications.

Why Hard Copy Submission Is Mandatory

Many colleges question the need for physical submission. AKTU requires hard copies for:

  • Official verification
  • Audit and record maintenance
  • Cross-checking ERP data
  • Examination transparency

The signed spiral-bound copy acts as the final institutional confirmation of internal marks.

Impact on Students

Although this notice is issued to colleges, students are directly affected.

Benefits for Students

  • Reduced risk of missing internal marks
  • Proper verification of scores
  • Smooth result declaration
  • Fair academic evaluation

Students should be aware that even though the AKTU internal marks upload date extended Odd Sem 2025–26, marks cannot be changed later once finalized.

What If Colleges Miss the Extended Deadline?

AKTU has not mentioned penalties explicitly, but based on past experience:

  • Internal marks may not be accepted
  • Student results can be delayed
  • Colleges may face official objections
  • Academic issues may arise

Hence, institutions must fully utilize the AKTU internal marks upload date extended for Odd Semester 2025–26 without delay.

Official AKTU Contact for Issues

For any technical or administrative issues related to internal marks uploading, AKTU has provided an official email:

📧 dcoe_b@aktu.ac.in

Colleges should clearly mention:

  • Institution name
  • Course and semester
  • Nature of problem
  • Supporting screenshots/documents

Issued By (Official Authority)

The notice regarding the AKTU internal marks upload date extended Odd Sem 2025–26 has been officially signed by:

Prof. Deepak Nagariya
Controller of Examination
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Lucknow

Important Points to Remember

  • Extension is final and time-bound
  • ERP upload and hard copy both compulsory
  • Colleges are responsible for accuracy
  • Students should confirm internal marks status

also read : AKTU Adecco Internship 2026: Who Can Apply, Stipend, Selection Process & CTC Details

Conclusion

The announcement that the AKTU internal marks upload date extended Odd Sem 2025–26 is a crucial academic update for colleges and students alike. With revised deadlines of 05 January 2026 (online upload) and 12 January 2026 (hard copy submission), institutions have sufficient time to complete internal assessment procedures correctly.

Colleges must act responsibly, and students should remain vigilant to ensure their internal marks are properly uploaded. Timely compliance with this notice will help avoid result delays and academic complications.

  • National and religious festivals
  • Special observance days

  • Prevents attendance-related issues

For Colleges and Faculty

The AKTU Minor Degree in Quantum Technologies is designed for students who want early exposure to quantum computing, quantum communication, quantum sensing, and quantum materials while continuing their main B.Tech degree.

This minor degree focuses on:

  • Multidisciplinary learning
  • Industry-oriented and research-driven skills

After successful completion, students will receive a Minor Degree in Quantum Technologies along with their UG degree from AKTU.

Why AKTU Introduced Minor Degree in Quantum Technologies?

AKTU introduced the AKTU Minor Degree in Quantum Technologies keeping in mind:

  • India’s National Quantum Mission (NQM)
  • Growing global demand for quantum professionals
  • NEP-2020 emphasis on flexible & skill-based education
  • Shortage of trained manpower in quantum domains

This programme aims to create a future-ready quantum workforce for India.

Eligibility Criteria for AKTU Minor Degree in Quantum Technologies

Students from all engineering branches are eligible.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Engineering Mathematics
  • Engineering Physics
  • Basic Programming Knowledge

This makes the AKTU Minor Degree in Quantum Technologies accessible to almost every B.Tech student.

Mandatory & Optional Courses

title.rendered: Cyber Challenge India Launches FREE eRaksha Hackathon 2026 – Free Certificate, Cash Prizes, Apply by 31 December

The FREE eRaksha Hackathon 2026 is a 36-hour innovation and prototype development challenge focused on defence-AI and digital security solutions.

This national-level event is being organised by eDC IIT Delhi in collaboration with CyberPeace Foundation. The objective is to develop scalable and practical cybersecurity technologies aligned with India’s national security needs.

Participants will work on real-world cybersecurity challenges such as:

Originality, uniqueness, and relevance to cybersecurity challenges.

title.rendered: How to Score 15–20 Extra Marks in University Exams: university exam answer writing tips

content.rendered:
Most students believe that marks only depend on how much you study. But in reality, university exams are a game of strategy, presentation, and smart writing. If you apply the right techniques while writing your paper, you can easily score 15–20 extra marks, even without studying everything in depth.

In this blog, I’ll explain 5 proven techniques that examiners actually expect from students. These methods work for any university(example – AKTU), any course, and any subject. If you seriously want to improve your results, read this till the end.

Why Answer Writing Matters More Than You Think

University exams are very different from school exams.
Here, examiners don’t just check what you write, but also how you write.

Many students fail or get backlogs because:

  • They leave questions unattempted
  • They don’t manage time
  • Their answer sheet looks messy
  • Answers are too short

That’s why learning university exam answer writing tips is just as important as studying the syllabus.

1. Time Management: Never Leave a Question Unattempted

Poor time management is the number one reason students lose marks.

After exams, you’ll often hear:

  • “I left 2 questions”
  • “15 marks ka question chhoot gaya”

In a university exam, leaving questions is a big mistake.

How to Manage Time Properly

  • Always carry a normal analog watch (digital watches are usually not allowed)
  • Before the exam, check:
    • Total questions
    • Total time (generally 3 hours = 180 minutes)

Example:

If there are 10 questions:

  • Each question ≈ 18 minutes

Keep this calculation in mind while writing.

Smart Exam Strategy

  • Decide a fixed time for each question
  • If time exceeds, move on
  • Write long questions first, short questions later

Even if you write slightly less, attempt every question. This single habit can save you from a backlog and is one of the most important university exam answer writing tips.

2. Margin and Spacing: First Impression Matters

Examiners judge your paper within the first few seconds.

Correct Margin Rules

  • Leave a normal margin on both left and right sides
  • Don’t leave too much space to fill pages artificially
  • Left and right margins should look balanced

Proper Spacing Between Answers

  • Leave 3 clear lines after finishing one question
  • Start the next answer clearly
  • This helps the examiner identify answers easily

Avoid These Mistakes

  • Writing on alternate lines
  • Giving too much space between words
  • Trying to “show pages” instead of content

Clean presentation is a silent scorer and a very underrated part of university exam answer writing tips.

3. Avoid Too Much Cutting and Scratching

Messy answer sheets directly reduce marks.

What Most Students Do Wrong

  • Cut full paragraphs
  • Overwrite sentences
  • Scratch aggressively

This draws the examiner’s attention to your mistakes.

Correct Way to Handle Errors

  • Small mistake? Ignore it
  • Big mistake?
    • Cut with one straight line only
    • Do not overwrite or scribble

A neat copy always creates a positive impression, which directly helps in scoring higher.

4. Write Answers the “University Way”, Not the School Way

This is where most students lose marks.

In school:

  • Correct answer in 5 lines = full marks

In university:

  • Same answer in 5 lines = very low marks

Golden Rule of University Exams

Marks = Content + Length + Structure

How to Expand Answers Smartly

Even if you know very little, you can still write 2–3 pages.

Step 1: Write whatever you know correctly
Step 2: Explain the same idea again in simple words
Step 3: Add related points like:

  • Explanation
  • Advantages
  • Applications
  • Examples

Never change your handwriting quality midway.
Consistency is one of the smartest university exam answer writing tips that students ignore.

5. Never Leave Any Question Blank

This rule alone can increase your marks drastically.

If you don’t know an answer:

  • Write something related to the topic
  • Use headings and points
  • Keep handwriting neat

For “Difference Between” Questions

  • Make two columns
  • Write 10–15 logical points
  • Even basic differences fetch marks

For Advantages / Disadvantages

  • Write 5–6 points each
  • Keep points relevant

Attempting every question is one of the most effective university exam answer writing tips for avoiding failure.

Bonus Tip: Use Only Blue Pen

  • Don’t switch between black and blue pens
  • Changing pens:
    • Wastes time
    • Attracts unnecessary attention

Use only blue pen for the entire paper.
It keeps your answer sheet uniform and clean.

Final Conclusion

University exams are not about perfection.
They are about smart execution.

If you apply these university exam answer writing tips properly:

  • You can score 15–20 extra marks
  • You can avoid backlogs
  • You can pass even tough papers confidently

Study smart, write smart, and trust the process.
These university exam answer writing tips have helped thousands of students—and they will help you too.

All the best for your university exams!

title.rendered: AKTU Odd Semester Exam 2025-26: आंशिक संशोधित परीक्षा कार्यक्रम जारी, ऑफलाइन परीक्षाएं 23 दिसंबर 2025 से

content.rendered:
AKTU Odd Semester Exam: डॉ. ए.पी.जे. अब्दुल कलाम प्राविधिक विश्वविद्यालय, लखनऊ (AKTU) ने शैक्षिक सत्र 2025-26 के विषम सेमेस्टर (Odd Semester) की परीक्षाओं को लेकर एक महत्वपूर्ण आधिकारिक सूचना जारी की है। विश्वविद्यालय द्वारा स्नातक (UG) और परास्नातक (PG) पाठ्यक्रमों में अध्ययनरत रेगुलर एवं कैरी ओवर छात्र-छात्राओं के लिए आंशिक संशोधित परीक्षा कार्यक्रम जारी किया गया है।

यह परीक्षा कार्यक्रम छात्रहित में प्राप्त अनुरोधों और सक्षम स्तर से प्राप्त अनुमोदन के बाद लागू किया गया है।

आधिकारिक सूचना का सार (Notice Highlights)

  • विश्वविद्यालय: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University
  • सत्र: 2025-26
  • सेमेस्टर: विषम सेमेस्टर (Odd Semester)
  • छात्र: UG एवं PG (Regular + Carry Over)
  • परीक्षा मोड: ऑफलाइन
  • परीक्षा तिथि: 23 दिसंबर 2025 से 31 जनवरी 2026 तक
  • सूचना जारी: परीक्षा नियंत्रक कार्यालय, AKTU
  • पत्रांक: AKTU/परीक्षा/2025/2442
  • दिनांक: 21 दिसंबर 2025

क्यों जारी किया गया आंशिक संशोधित परीक्षा कार्यक्रम?

विश्वविद्यालय को विभिन्न संस्थानों एवं छात्र-छात्राओं की ओर से छात्रहित में अनुरोध प्राप्त हुए थे। इन अनुरोधों पर विचार करते हुए, सक्षम प्राधिकारी से अनुमोदन के पश्चात यह आंशिक संशोधन जारी किया गया है ताकि:

  • परीक्षाओं का संचालन सुचारु हो
  • छात्रों को उचित समय और बेहतर तैयारी का अवसर मिले
  • संस्थानों को परीक्षा संचालन में सहयोग प्राप्त हो

किन परीक्षाओं पर लागू होगा यह संशोधन Odd Semester ?

यह संशोधित परीक्षा कार्यक्रम निम्न पर लागू होगा:

  • सभी UG (B.Tech, B.Pharm, B.Arch आदि)
  • सभी PG (M.Tech, MBA, MCA आदि)
  • Regular छात्र
  • Carry Over / Back Paper छात्र

नोट: संशोधन आंशिक है, यानी सभी विषयों में नहीं बल्कि कुछ चयनित विषयों/तिथियों में बदलाव किया गया है।

कॉलेजों और संस्थानों के लिए निर्देश

AKTU द्वारा संबद्ध समस्त संस्थानों को निर्देशित किया गया है कि:

  • इस सूचना को छात्र/छात्राओं तक तत्काल पहुंचाएं
  • संशोधित कार्यक्रम के अनुसार परीक्षा से संबंधित आवश्यक कार्यवाही समय से करें
  • विषम सेमेस्टर परीक्षा के आयोजन में पूर्ण सहयोग प्रदान करें
  • ERP, परीक्षा शाखा एवं मीडिया/जनसम्पर्क से समन्वय बनाए रखें

छात्रों के लिए महत्वपूर्ण सलाह

छात्रों को निम्न बातों का विशेष ध्यान रखना चाहिए:

  • अपना संशोधित परीक्षा कार्यक्रम विश्वविद्यालय/कॉलेज की वेबसाइट से अवश्य चेक करें
  • परीक्षा केंद्र, विषय कोड और तिथि की दोबारा पुष्टि करें
  • एडमिट कार्ड में दिए गए निर्देशों का पालन करें
  • किसी भी भ्रम की स्थिति में कॉलेज परीक्षा विभाग से संपर्क करें

परीक्षा नियंत्रक द्वारा जारी सूचना

यह सूचना परीक्षा नियंत्रक, AKTU (पूर्ववर्ती उत्तर प्रदेश प्राविधिक विश्वविद्यालय) द्वारा जारी की गई है और इसकी प्रतिलिपि:

  • प्रतिकुलपति
  • कुलसचिव
  • वित्त अधिकारी
  • संयुक्त/उप परीक्षा नियंत्रक
  • जनसम्पर्क अधिकारी / मीडिया प्रभारी
  • ERP प्रभारी

को आवश्यक कार्यवाही एवं सूचना हेतु प्रेषित की गई है।

READ MORE : AKTU Exam Advisory on Answer Booklet Usage for Odd Semester

निष्कर्ष (Conclusion)

title.rendered: AKTU Exam Advisory on Answer Booklet Usage for Odd Semester

content.rendered:
AKTU Exam Advisory on Answer Booklet Usage for Odd Semester: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Lucknow has released an important advisory for students in connection with the conduct of examinations for the academic session 2025–26. The notice has been issued to preserve the dignity, impartiality, and discipline of the university examination system.

This advisory holds special significance for students appearing in the AKTU Odd Semester Exam 2025–26.

Official Direction from the University Authorities

The university administration has formally instructed that no examinee shall write any form of personal identification inside the answer booklet. The answer book is meant solely for academic evaluation and must not contain any information that reveals the identity of the candidate.

The instruction has been issued by Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Technical University and shall be strictly enforced during the AKTU Odd Semester Exam 2025–26.

Prohibited Information Inside Answer Books

Candidates are strictly advised not to mention or indicate any of the following details on the inner pages of the answer booklet:

  • Mobile or telephone number
  • Roll number
  • Residential or postal address
  • Email ID
  • Any symbol, sign, or mark that may indicate identity
  • Any message or note intended for the examiner

The answer booklet must remain anonymous to ensure unbiased evaluation.

Disciplinary Action in Case of Violation

The university has cautioned that violation of these instructions shall be treated as adoption of Unfair Means (UFM). Such cases will be examined under UFM Rule Clause B (05).

Mentioning personal details may be construed as an attempt to influence the examiner. In such situations, the responsibility shall lie entirely with the student, and disciplinary action, including cancellation of examination results, may be initiated. This warning has been clearly emphasized for the AKTU Odd Semester Exam 2025–26.

Examination Period Information

As notified by the university, the odd semester written examinations shall be conducted during the following period:

The above instructions shall remain applicable throughout the entire duration of the AKTU Odd Semester Exam 2025–26.

Instructions to Colleges and Examination Centres

All affiliated colleges and examination centres have been directed to inform students of these rules in advance and ensure strict compliance during the examination process. Institutional authorities are expected to maintain vigilance and uphold examination discipline.

Students appearing in the AKTU Odd Semester Exam 2025–26 are advised to follow all instructions with due seriousness.

Guidance for Examinees

Candidates are advised to observe the following points carefully:

  • Write only subject-related answers
  • Fill in roll numbers only at the designated place
  • Avoid writing messages, appeals, or personal remarks
  • Maintain decorum and discipline throughout the examination

Even a minor oversight may lead to severe consequences.

Concluding Statement

The university has clarified that these instructions are issued not as a punitive measure, but to safeguard the fairness and credibility of the evaluation system. Adherence to these guidelines will ensure smooth conduct of examinations and impartial assessment of answer scripts.

Students are therefore urged to act responsibly and comply fully with the rules laid down for the AKTU Odd Semester Exam 2025–26.

Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow has issued an important official notification for all affiliated institutions regarding the submission of internal assessment marks for the Odd Semester of the Academic Session 2025–26. This announcement is critical for ensuring timely result processing and accurate academic records.

What Is the AKTU Odd Semester Internal Marks 2025–26 Notification?

The AKTU Odd Semester Internal Marks 2025–26 notification explains the procedure and deadlines for uploading Theory and Practical Sessional marks for students enrolled in Undergraduate and Postgraduate programs. The university has activated the ERP Portal to enable online submission by affiliated colleges.

Eligible Courses and Students

This notification applies to:

  • Undergraduate (UG) students
  • Postgraduate (PG) students
  • Students appearing in Regular and Carry Over subjects

B.Pharm First Semester students are not included in the AKTU Odd Semester Internal Marks 2025–26 process.

ERP Portal and Online Submission Deadline

Affiliated institutions must upload internal assessment marks for Theory Sessional and Practical Sessional subjects through the ERP portal.

The last date for online submission is 31 December 2025. Timely compliance with this deadline is mandatory under the AKTU Odd Semester Internal Marks 2025–26 guidelines.

Hard Copy Submission Instructions

In addition to online uploading, institutions are required to submit signed and verified hard copies of both internal and external marks. All documents must be spiral-bound and authenticated.

The deadline for submitting hard copies is 05 January 2026. These documents must be submitted to the Office of the Controller of Examinations, AKTU, Lucknow, as mandated in the AKTU Odd Semester Internal Marks 2025–26 notification.

Record Preservation Guidelines

All affiliated colleges are instructed to securely preserve internal marks data and related documents. These records must be made available to the university whenever required for audit or verification related to the AKTU Odd Semester Internal Marks 2025–26.

Contact for Technical or Administrative Issues

If any institution encounters technical or administrative difficulties during the process, they may contact the university via email at dcoe_b@aktu.ac.in. This communication channel has been provided specifically for matters concerning the AKTU Odd Semester Internal Marks 2025–26.

Instructions to Directors and Principals

Directors and Principals of all AKTU-affiliated institutions are requested to inform students about this notification and ensure that all procedures are completed within the prescribed timeline. Controller of Examinations
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Lucknow

content.rendered:

What is UP Dashmottar Scholarship 2025–26?

The UP Dashmottar Scholarship 2025–26 is a post-matric scholarship scheme run by the Uttar Pradesh government for students studying after Class 10. Under this scheme, eligible students receive:

  • Scholarship amount
  • Fee reimbursement
  • Direct benefit transfer (DBT) to their bank account through PFMS

This scheme mainly benefits students from:

  • General category (economically weaker students)
  • Other Backward Classes (OBC)
  • Minority communities

Why Was the UP Dashmottar Scholarship 2025–26 Schedule Revised?

According to the official notice, the revised schedule was issued because:

  • Master data was not locked on time in many districts

The revised schedule of UP Dashmottar Scholarship 2025–26 gives students:

The UP Dashmottar Scholarship 2025–26 revised schedule is a crucial update for students pursuing higher education in Uttar Pradesh. If you are eligible, make sure you apply on time, track your application regularly, and stay in touch with your institution.

Missing even one step can delay or cancel your scholarship, so stay alert and informed.

Lucknow: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow has issued an important official notification regarding the AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26 for the Odd Semester. The notice has been released by the Controller of Examination and circulated to all affiliated colleges and institutions. Through this notification, the university has directed colleges to conduct practical and project examinations on priority and ensure the timely online uploading of marks and mandatory documents.

The university has clearly stated that practical and project examinations are a compulsory academic component. Any delay or negligence in following the instructions may directly affect students’ results and academic progress.

Official Statement from Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University

According to the official circular, all undergraduate and postgraduate programs running under AKTU must strictly follow the guidelines issued for the AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26. The university has emphasized transparency, discipline, and timely completion of practical and project examinations across all affiliated institutions.

What Is AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26

The AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26 refers to the practical and project examinations conducted for students enrolled in the Odd Semester of the academic session 2025–26. These examinations are applicable to students appearing in regular subjects as well as those appearing in carry over or back paper subjects.

Marks obtained in the AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26 are combined with theory marks and play a crucial role in the preparation of semester results. Therefore, both students and colleges must treat these exams with seriousness.

Key Details of AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26

Timeline Announced for AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26

As per the notification, colleges have been instructed to start practical and project examinations immediately. The university has fixed a maximum duration of one week to complete all practical and project exams.

AKTU has also clarified that the AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26 must be completed before the end of written theory examinations. This step has been taken to ensure smooth result processing and avoid unnecessary delays in result declaration.

Guidelines for Conducting Practical and Project Exams

The university has issued strict instructions regarding the conduct of the AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26 to maintain uniformity and fairness.

AKTU has clearly mentioned that late uploading of marks will not be accepted under any circumstances. Colleges will be fully responsible for any delay or error.

Mandatory Geo-Tagged Photograph Instructions

To ensure transparency during the AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26, colleges are required to upload three geo-tagged group photographs.

Each photograph must clearly show students along with internal and external examiners. Geo-tagging must be enabled, and photographs must be uploaded only through the AKTU ERP portal.

AKTU has also instructed colleges to securely preserve all records related to the AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26. These records include practical answer sheets, project evaluation reports, examiner details, and other supporting documents.

Colleges must keep these records safe and produce them whenever demanded by the university for verification or inspection purposes.

Important Advisory for Students

Students appearing in the AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26 are advised to remain alert and informed. Practical examinations play a major role in the final result and overall academic performance.

Students should ensure:

  • They attend practical exams on time
  • They follow all instructions given by examiners
  • They cooperate during geo-tag photograph capture
  • They avoid any unfair practices

Official Help and Contact Information

In case of any technical or procedural issue related to the AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26, colleges can contact the university through the official email address:

dcoe_b@aktu.ac.in

Conclusion

The latest notice issued by AKTU makes it clear that the AKTU Practical Exam 2025–26 is a high-priority academic activity. Colleges must conduct exams within the given timeline, upload marks and geo-tagged photographs on time, and preserve all related records carefully. Students must also stay informed and participate responsibly.

content.rendered:
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow has officially released an important notice regarding AKTU PG Dissertation Evaluation 2024–25. This update is based on the official circular issued on 17 December 2025 and is applicable to M.Tech, M.Pharm and M.Arch (MURP) courses.

All regular and carry-over postgraduate students must carefully read and follow this update to avoid rejection of their dissertation.

What Is the AKTU PG Dissertation Evaluation 2024–25 Update?

According to the official notice shared by AKTU, the university has clearly explained how AKTU PG Dissertation Evaluation 2024–25 will be conducted. The notice mainly focuses on:

Offline dissertation evaluation and viva
Mandatory plagiarism check using Turnitin
Correct thesis formatting as per AKTU guidelines
ERP upload process and deadline

This update applies to students registered in sessions 2020–21 to 2024–25.

Dissertation Evaluation and Viva Will Be Offline

One of the most important points of AKTU PG Dissertation Evaluation 2024–25 is that the dissertation evaluation and viva-voce examination will be conducted in OFFLINE mode.

This rule applies to:
M.Tech students
M.Pharm students
M.Arch / MURP students

Students must appear physically for the viva as per the schedule provided by their institute.

Plagiarism Check Is Compulsory for AKTU PG Dissertation Evaluation 2024–25

AKTU has made it very clear that plagiarism checking is mandatory for all PG dissertations.

For AKTU PG Dissertation Evaluation 2024–25, students must:

  • Use Turnitin software only
  • Follow plagiarism guidelines issued on 22 July 2020
  • Submit a Turnitin plagiarism report
  • Submit a Certificate of Non-Plagiarism signed by the supervisor and forwarded by the institute

Students must ensure that their thesis is not uploaded to any public repository during plagiarism checking, as this can increase similarity and lead to rejection.

AKTU Can Re-Check and Reject the Dissertation

Under AKTU PG Dissertation Evaluation 2024–25, the university has the authority to re-check dissertations at its own level using Turnitin.

If the dissertation does not follow plagiarism rules or formatting guidelines, AKTU can reject it and take action against:
The student
The supervisor
The institute

Dissertation Formatting Rules Are Mandatory

Only those dissertations will be accepted under AKTU PG Dissertation Evaluation 2024–25 that strictly follow:

  • AKTU thesis formatting rules
  • Ph.D / M.Tech / M.Pharm thesis preparation guidelines available on the AKTU website

If formatting is incorrect, the dissertation will not be accepted for evaluation.

ERP Upload Dates for AKTU PG Dissertation Evaluation 2024–25

As per the official notice images, the ERP upload process is time-bound.

  • ERP upload start date: 18 December 2025
  • Last date for upload: 30 December 2025

The institute will upload the student application using Director ERP Login. Students must:

  • Fill all information correctly
  • Upload the complete thesis in MS Word format
  • Pay the required dissertation fee through ERP

Without fee payment, the application for AKTU PG Dissertation Evaluation 2024–25 will be rejected.

Important Instructions Mentioned in the Notice

  • The official notice clearly states that:
  • The complete thesis must be uploaded with cover page
  • All documents must be uploaded as a single file
  • Plagiarism guidelines must be followed strictly

If these instructions are not followed, the dissertation will not be accepted, and responsibility will lie with the student, supervisor, and institute.

What Should Students Do Now?

Students appearing under AKTU PG Dissertation Evaluation 2024–25 should immediately:

  • Contact their guide and college
  • Complete Turnitin plagiarism checking early
  • Verify thesis format carefully
  • Avoid last-minute ERP submission

Final Words

The AKTU PG Dissertation Evaluation 2024–25 notice is extremely important for all M.Tech, M.Pharm, and M.Arch students. Any mistake in plagiarism checking, formatting, or ERP submission can lead to rejection of the dissertation.

Students are advised to strictly follow the official notice and complete all formalities within the given timeline.

title.rendered: AKTU Virtual Internship Program 2026 Announced: Free 60-Hour Internship Begins January 19, Apply Before January 15

content.rendered:
Lucknow | December 19, 2025

Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow has officially announced the AKTU Virtual Internship Program 2026, offering students a free 60-hour virtual internship in multiple emerging technology domains. The internship will commence from 19 January 2026, and registrations are now open for students of all AKTU-affiliated and associated colleges.

The announcement of the AKTU Virtual Internship Program 2026 has been made through an official circular issued by Prof. Neelam Srivastava, Dean – Training & Placement, AKTU. The notification has been circulated to all college directors and principals with a request to ensure maximum participation from students.

This initiative is being seen as a major step by AKTU to strengthen industry exposure, skill development, and project-based learning among students, without any financial burden.

What Is AKTU Virtual Internship Program 2026?

The AKTU Virtual Internship Program 2026 is a structured online internship designed to provide students with real-world skills through a blend of live expert sessions, self-paced learning, and hands-on project work. The program focuses on new and emerging technology tracks, enabling students to gain practical knowledge aligned with current industry requirements.

Unlike traditional internships that are limited to specific branches or paid programs, the AKTU Virtual Internship Program 2026 is open to students from any course or department and is completely free of cost.

The university aims to bridge the gap between classroom learning and industry expectations through this well-planned internship model.

Total Duration and Structure of the Internship

The AKTU Virtual Internship Program 2026 consists of a total of 60 hours, carefully divided to ensure balanced learning and application.

Live Sessions (20 Hours)

Students will attend live online sessions conducted by industry experts. These sessions focus on conceptual understanding, real-world use cases, and interaction with mentors.

Self-Paced Learning (20 Hours)

This component allows flexibility, enabling students to learn at their own pace through recorded content and guided modules provided under the AKTU Virtual Internship Program 2026.

Project Development (20 Hours)

title.rendered: IGNOU UGC-MMTTC Announces 8-Day Online NEP 2020 Orientation Programme from December 17

content.rendered:
New Delhi, December 2025:
The UGC–Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Centre (MMTTC), IGNOU, has announced an Eight Days Online NEP 2020 Orientation & Sensitization Programme, scheduled to be conducted from 17 December to 29 December 2025. The programme is being organized under the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Programme (MMTTP) of the Ministry of Education, Government of India.

The initiative aims to strengthen the understanding and practical implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 among teachers, researchers, and academic professionals across higher education institutions in India.

Programme Details at a Glance

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

The programme is open to:

  • Faculty members of universities and colleges
  • Research Associates
  • Research Scholars
  • Post-Doctoral Fellows
  • Other academic professionals

Applicants must upload a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their institution. Selection will be done on a first-come, first-served basis.

Key Focus Areas of the NEP 2020 Programme

The training will cover major academic and policy-driven themes aligned with NEP 2020, including:

  • Higher Education and Society
  • Holistic and Multidisciplinary Education
  • Indian Knowledge Systems
  • Research and Development
  • Curriculum Design, Pedagogy, and Assessment
  • Skill Development and Employability
  • Inclusive Education and Student Diversity
  • ICT in Education and Innovative Teaching Practices
  • Academic Leadership and Governance
  • Teaching–Learning through Mother/Local Languages
  • Cyber Security Awareness
  • Mental Health and Well-being
  • Institutional Autonomy and Student Choice

Mode of Training

  • Sessions will be conducted entirely online
  • Resource persons will include senior faculty and experts from IGNOU, Central Universities, and National Institutions
  • The programme will emphasize interactive learning, discussion, and experience sharing

Application Process Explained

Interested participants can apply through the UGC Malaviya Mission portal by following these steps:

  1. Register as a participant at: https://mmc.ugc.ac.in/registration/Index
  2. Login at: https://mmc.ugc.ac.in/Login/Index
  3. Select Centre: Indira Gandhi National Open University, New Delhi
  4. Choose Month: December 2025
  5. Download and upload the prescribed NOC/Nomination Letter
  6. Select Programme Dates: 17-12-2025 to 29-12-2025
  7. Enter Programme ID: MMC-142-2025-DEC-A-07287
  8. Click on Participate and confirm

Why This Programme Matters

With NEP 2020 driving major reforms in higher education, this orientation programme is designed to equip educators with policy clarity, academic leadership skills, and practical insights required to implement NEP-aligned reforms at institutional levels. Participants completing the programme are expected to contribute actively to curriculum innovation and governance reforms.

Programme Coordinators

  • Dr. Hemlata Baghel
    Assistant Professor, STRIDE, IGNOU
    Email: hemlatabaghel@ignou.ac.in
  • Prof. Amiteshwar Ratra
    Professor, STRIDE, IGNOU
    Email: amiteshwar@ignou.ac.in

For general queries: mmttcstride@ignou.ac.in

Final Note

Higher education institutions are encouraged to nominate eligible faculty members and academic professionals before the deadline to ensure participation in this nationally significant NEP 2020 capacity-building initiative.

Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU) has issued a crucial notification for all its affiliated institutions regarding the Post-Matric Scholarship and Fee Reimbursement Scheme for the academic session 2025-26. As per the latest university order, colleges must complete the online verification of scholarship applications and actual student strength by December 18, 2025.

The directive, issued from the university headquarters in Lucknow, follows instructions from the Social Welfare Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh, and applies to both government and self-financed institutions.

The university has clearly stated that AKTU Scholarship Verification 2025-26 is mandatory to ensure timely disbursement of scholarship and fee reimbursement amounts to eligible students.

Online Verification Made Mandatory for All Affiliated Colleges

According to the official notice, AKTU has directed institutions to verify the authenticity of students’ online scholarship applications along with the real number of students currently enrolled. This step has been introduced to prevent discrepancies, ineligible claims, and duplication under multiple scholarship schemes.

The AKTU Scholarship Verification 2025-26 process will be carried out entirely online and must be completed within the prescribed timeline without any exception.

Affidavit Submission Required from Director or Principal

In addition to online verification, the university has made it compulsory for the Director or Principal of each affiliated institution to submit a signed affidavit. Through this affidavit, the institution must certify that:

  • All forwarded students are genuinely enrolled in the institution
  • All scholarship applications have been properly verified
  • Only eligible students’ applications have been forwarded
  • No student has applied under any other Central Government scholarship scheme
  • No ineligible student has been included in the list

AKTU has warned that if any false information or irregularity is found at a later stage, the concerned institution will be held fully responsible.

December 18 Deadline Is Strict, Warns AKTU

The university has emphasized that December 18, 2025 is the final date for completing the verification and submitting the affidavit. Failure to meet this deadline may result in delays or cancellation of scholarship benefits for students.

Officials clarified that any consequences arising from late submission or incorrect verification under AKTU Scholarship Verification 2025-26 will be borne entirely by the institution concerned.

Advisory Issued for Students

AKTU has also advised students to remain vigilant and coordinate closely with their respective colleges. Students should regularly check the status of their scholarship applications and ensure that all details submitted online are accurate and complete.

Incorrect or mismatched information may lead to rejection or delayed processing of scholarship payments under AKTU Scholarship Verification 2025-26.

  • Scheme: Post-Matric Scholarship and Fee Reimbursement
  • Academic Session: 2025-26
  • Verification Mode: Online
  • Last Date: December 18, 2025
  • Applicable Institutions: Government and Self-Financed Colleges
  • Responsible Authority: Director / Principal

Final Word

The latest AKTU notification makes it clear that AKTU Scholarship Verification 2025-26 is a critical step in ensuring transparency and timely release of scholarship funds. Institutions and students are strongly advised to complete all required formalities well before the deadline to avoid last-minute issues.

https://forms.gle/a4J2wp8dfzWivi5D7

Institutions are advised to recheck placement numbers carefully before final submission to avoid data mismatch or future correspondence from the university.

This data collection exercise will help the government assess the placement performance of AKTU-affiliated institutions, understand employability trends, and plan future technical education policies in Uttar Pradesh.

All directors and principals are advised to immediately coordinate with their Training and Placement Cells and ensure AKTU placement data submission 2025 is completed well before the deadline to avoid last-minute issues.
